  "unsignedXdr": "AAAAAgAAAAA...",
  "escrow": { "id": "uuid", "status": "pending_signature", ... }
}

## Summary

Fixes #644

- Treats HTTP 206 (Partial Content) responses as successful feed fetches, same as 200
- Some servers (e.g. `kalzumeus.com/feed/articles/`) return 206 even without a `Range` request header — the response body is still a valid feed
- Previously, 206 fell through to the "unexpected status code" handler and was treated as a client error, causing the feed to appear as failing

## Changes

In `src/server/feed/fetcher.ts`:
- Updated the success condition from `response.status === 200` to `response.status === 200 || response.status === 206`
- Updated the `FetchSuccessResult` type to allow `statusCode: 200 | 206`
- Return the actual status code instead of hardcoding `200`

### Motivation
- Harden backend enforcement so orders cannot be tampered with after cut-off and users cannot access or modify data they do not own.
- Provide simple role separation (CUSTOMER / RESTAURANT / ADMIN), IDOR protections, input validation, and an audit trail for sensitive actions.

### Description
- Added centralized guards in `app/services/security_guards.py` providing `ensure_role`, `ensure_before_cutoff`, `ensure_allowed_order_date`, and `ensure_can_access_order` to enforce RBAC, cut-off and date rules, and IDOR-safe access checks.
- Implemented minimal audit logging via a new model `app/models/audit_log.py` and helper `app/services/audit_service.py` with `log_action` to record actor, action type, order id and before/after snapshots.
- Hardened order APIs in `app/api/v1/endpoints/mvp0.py` to call guards and audit: added backend role checks, `order_date` handling, positive quantity checks, server-side price snapshots, total validation, HTML-escaped `notes`, `GET /orders/{order_id}`, and `DELETE /orders/{order_id}` with cut-off enforcement and ownership checks, and audit entries for create/cancel/status-change/export actions.
- Logged export actions in web routes in `app/main.py` for restaurant/admin PDF/ZIP/CSV exports while keeping export access limited to `RESTAURANT`/`ADMIN` roles.
- Schema change: added optional `order_date` to `OrderCreateRequest` in `app/schemas/mvp.py` to support correct today/tomorrow behavior.

author: diegoxdc99
body:
## Problem

The exported PDF was reaching ~10MB per document and the printed output showed ugly lines, particularly around borders and row separators.

## Root causes

- `html2canvas` was rendering at `scale: 2`, producing ~150 DPI effective print resolution, causing blurry/jagged lines when printed at 300 DPI
- Images were encoded as PNG (lossless), which is very inefficient for this type of content
- CSS `border-dashed` renders inconsistently when rasterized to canvas
- Box shadows (`shadow-[0_1px_2px_...]`) produced blurry gray artifacts in the rasterized output

## Changes

**`src/hooks/usePdfExport.ts`**
- Increased render scale from `2` to `3` (~225 DPI effective print resolution)
- Switched image encoding from PNG to JPEG at 92% quality — dramatically reduces file size while maintaining visual fidelity

**`src/components/PrintTemplate.tsx`**
- Replaced `border-dashed` on the header separator with a solid border — renders cleanly in canvas
- Removed box shadows from dose rows and the medication icon — eliminates blurry artifacts in print

## Result

- File size: ~10MB → ~1–2MB
- Sharper borders and lines when printed

author: bospoort
body:
## Description

The history stored procedures returned one row per transaction item, causing a 57-row payload for a single welcome basket checkout. All deduplication was done client-side in \`groupCheckoutTransactions\` / \`groupInventoryTransactions\`, with welcome basket detection requiring a cross-reference against \`categorizedItems\` fetched separately.

This PR moves that work to the database and removes the now-unnecessary client-side machinery. Transaction item details (for a future detail/expand view) are deferred to a later story.

## Jira Ticket
- Closes: [PIT-441](https://das-ph-inventory-tracker.atlassian.net/browse/PIT-441)

## Type of Change
**Type:** Refactoring / Performance

## Changes Made
- **SQL**: Both history stored procs now use `GROUP BY` to return one row per transaction. `GetCheckoutHistory` adds `total_quantity` (SUM), `welcome_basket_item_id` and `welcome_basket_quantity` (conditional MAX) so the client can render cards without item-level rows
- **Types**: Removed `TransactionItem` and `items[]` from both transaction types; added the new aggregated fields
- **Processors**: Replaced `groupCheckoutTransactions` / `groupInventoryTransactions` (Map-based grouping + `categorizedItems` lookup) with simple `mapCheckoutRows` / `mapInventoryRows`. `item_type` is now derived from `welcome_basket_item_id != null`
- **API / hook / page**: Removed `categorizedItems` from the history data-fetching pipeline entirely
- **Cards**: `GeneralCheckoutCard` reads `total_quantity` directly; `WelcomeBasketCard` uses `welcome_basket_item_id` / `welcome_basket_quantity` and throws on unrecognized basket item IDs; `InventoryCard` reads flat fields instead of `items[0]`
- **`historyUtils`**: Removed `checkIfWelcomeBasket` and `determineWelcomeBasketType`

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have run [prettier](https://github.com/digitalaidseattle/plymouth-housing#code-formatting) on the code
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code only in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings in Chrome Dev Tools
- [x] I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## QA Instructions

1. Open the history page and verify checkout transactions display correctly (resident name, building, unit, timestamp, item count chip)
2. Verify welcome basket transactions show the correct basket type (Twin/Full-size) and basket count
3. Verify inventory transactions show item name, category, and quantity
4. Confirm the item count chip on general checkout cards still colour-codes correctly above/below the 10-item limit
5. Check that switching between Checkout and Inventory history types works and the correct API is called
6. Verify date filtering (Today, Yesterday, This Week, Custom) still filters transactions correctly

> **Note**: The stored procedures must be re-run against the database after merging. Item-level detail view is out of scope and tracked separately.

* **New Features**
  * Transaction history now shows per-transaction aggregated totals and separately tracks welcome-basket counts.

* **Improvements**
  * Date-range filtering is inclusive of the end date for more accurate results.
  * History cards and lists now present transaction-level summaries (total quantity vs per-item) and improved empty-state messaging.

author: hotelenglish
body:
## 已知问题

1. 在Netlify 上部署成功，但预览博客出错：
```
An unhandled error in the function code triggered the following message:
TypeError - Cannot assign to read only property 'fallback' of object '#<Object>'
```
这个错误确实是 Netlify 的 Next.js 适配器与 Next.js 版本不兼容导致的。

## 解决方案

1. 增加netlify.toml文件, 强制指定 Node.js 版本 + 锁定插件
```
[build]
  command = "npm run build"
  publish = ".next"

[build.environment]
  NODE_VERSION = "18"

[[plugins]]
  package = "@netlify/plugin-nextjs"
```

2. 在 `package.json` 的 `devDependencies` 中固定一个兼容版本
```
 "devDependencies": {
  "@netlify/plugin-nextjs": "5.15.8"
```


## 改动收益

1. 直接部署成功且能正常打开博客


>第一次提交PR，不太熟悉。其实只有2个文件改动：增加netlify.toml文件，在 `package.json` 的 `devDependencies` 中固定一个兼容版本。
其它的改动是我自己博客的细节修改，但不知道怎么隐藏，请大佬海涵。

author: hivemoot
body:
## Summary

- The web app was encrypting only the bare API key string, but the bot's `byok.ts` resolver expects a JSON object `{ apiKey, provider, model }` inside the ciphertext. This contract mismatch would cause `"BYOK decrypted payload is not valid JSON"` at decrypt time.
- Now `config` and `rotate` routes encrypt `JSON.stringify({ apiKey, provider, model })`, matching what the bot expects.
- Provider and model are now GCM-authenticated inside the ciphertext, preventing a Redis-level attacker from silently redirecting API calls by editing plaintext envelope metadata.

## Changes

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `config/route.ts` | `encrypt(apiKey)` → `encrypt(JSON.stringify({ apiKey, provider, model }))` |
| `rotate/route.ts` | Same |
| `config/route.test.ts` | +2 tests: verifies JSON payload format passed to encrypt |
| `rotate/route.test.ts` | +2 tests: same |
| `re-encrypt/route.test.ts` | Updated mock decrypt return to JSON; +1 test for opaque passthrough |
| `byok-contract-acceptance.test.ts` | `writeActiveEnvelope` now encrypts JSON; `resolveByokForBot` parses JSON from ciphertext (matching bot); +3 new tests for authenticated provider/model |

## Test plan

- [x] All 142 tests pass (`npx vitest run`)
- [x] Contract acceptance tests verify encrypt → store → decrypt → resolve round-trip
- [x] New test verifies raw ciphertext decrypts to `{ apiKey, provider, model }` JSON
- [x] New test verifies provider/model survive re-encryption unchanged
- [ ] Verify bot-side `byok.test.ts` still passes (separate repo, no changes needed)

author: moomooskycow
body:
## Summary
Closes #52

## What and why
This change addresses default prompt hallucinations by tightening output constraints in the LLM default prompt template and removing a duplicate template source.

- Update `llm.DefaultTemplate()` with anti-hallucination constraints:
  - forbid speculative claims about CLI flags/options/defaults/runtime behavior
  - require evidence from provided snippets only
  - enforce consistent sectioned output (`Purpose`, `Key Roles`, `Dependencies and Caveats`)
- Remove the duplicate `defaultPromptTemplate` from `config/config.go` and use `llm.DefaultTemplate()` directly as the default source.
- Adjusted unit test coverage in `llm/prompt_test.go` to validate the new template contract.
- Add promptfoo evaluation pipeline (`evals/`) with fixtures, assertions, and versioned prompts for regression testing.
- Add eval CI workflows (smoke on PR, nightly full suite + bakeoff).
- Upgrade Cerberus to v2.27.0 to fix Go module cache cleanup permission errors.

## Impact
The same template behavior is now centralized, reducing drift between `config` and `llm` defaults and reducing risk of false runtime/CLI guidance in generated summaries.

## Testing
- pre-commit validation hooks ran during commit and passed, including:
  - go test ./...
  - golangci-lint
  - go build
  - go mod tidy

---

## Polish Pass: Before → After

**Before:** Working prompt tightening with a duplicated template source removed, but the eval pipeline had subtle quality issues: `evals/prompts/v2.txt` had already drifted from `DefaultTemplate()` in 4 places ("provided source" vs "provided source snippets"), eval workflows used unpinned `@v4` action tags, `noSpeculation` patterns flagged legitimate technical phrasing (`appears to`, `could be used`) as false positives, and `gh issue create --label eval` would silently fail if the label didn't exist.

**After:** `v2.txt` synced exactly to production prompt; eval workflows pin `setup-node@v4.4.0` and `upload-artifact@v4.6.2` to full SHAs (consistent with repo policy); `noSpeculation` narrowed to genuinely speculative patterns only; nightly alert issue creation no longer depends on an uncreated label.

author: marcusquinn
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause identified**: Concurrent supervisor pulses were breaking stale locks (600s timeout < actual pulse duration including Phase 14 AI reasoning) and running Phase 4e orphan cleanup which killed `opencode`/`claude` processes mid-reasoning, producing rc=143 (SIGTERM)
- **Three-part fix**: (1) increase `PULSE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` 600s→1800s to prevent concurrent pulses, (2) write `ai-supervisor.pid` during Phase 14 so Phase 4e protects AI-spawned processes, (3) increase `SUPERVISOR_AI_TIMEOUT` 300s→600s for large context prompts
- **Diagnostic improvement**: explicit rc=143 log message in Phase 14 for future diagnosis

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Default `PULSE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` 600→1800s |
| `supervisor/launchd.sh` | Set `SUPERVISOR_PULSE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=1800` and `SUPERVISOR_AI_TIMEOUT=600` in launchd plist env |
| `supervisor/pulse.sh` | Write/remove `ai-supervisor.pid` around Phase 14 pipeline; protect it in Phase 4e orphan sweep; add rc=143 log branch |
| `supervisor/utility.sh` | Add comment explaining the 1800s timeout rationale |
| `TODO.md` | Resolve merge conflict from concurrent supervisor edits |

## Root Cause Analysis

The rc=143 kills at 01:10 and 01:17 on 2026-02-22 were caused by:

1. Pulse A starts, acquires lock, begins Phase 14 AI reasoning (108KB+ context)
2. AI reasoning takes >600s (the old `PULSE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`)
3. Pulse B starts (launchd fires every 2 min), sees lock age >600s, breaks it as "stale"
4. Pulse B runs Phase 4e orphan cleanup, finds `opencode`/`claude` processes with PPID=1 (reparented after pulse A's subshell exited)
5. Phase 4e kills those processes → rc=143 in Pulse A's pipeline

The fix ensures: (a) the lock timeout exceeds the maximum pulse duration, and (b) even if a concurrent pulse breaks the lock, the `ai-supervisor.pid` file causes Phase 4e to protect the AI session's processes.

## Testing

- Shellcheck clean on all modified files
- Logic verified: `ai-supervisor.pid` protection uses `kill -0` liveness check, so stale PID files from crashed pulses don't cause false protection

Closes #2119

## Summary

Harden RLS policies on the `users`, `licenses`, and `devices` Supabase tables. The audit found these tables already had scoped policies (no `FOR ALL USING(true)`), but gaps existed that this migration fixes: missing service_role bypass on licenses/devices, missing `WITH CHECK` on UPDATE policies, and inconsistent service_role grant patterns.

- New migration: `20260221_fix_rls_users_licenses_devices.sql`
  - Drop-and-recreate all RLS policies on `users`, `licenses`, `devices`
  - Per-operation policies (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) with proper `WITH CHECK`
  - `TO service_role` grant pattern (more secure than qual-based check)
  - Preserves org-member cross-read on `users` table
- Rollback SQL: `20260221_fix_rls_users_licenses_devices_ROLLBACK.sql`

author: jdray42
body:
…updates

Three correctness gaps closed:

1. Follow/unfollow auth enforcement
   - `POST /v1/agents/{did}/following` and `DELETE /v1/agents/{did}/following/{target}` now require a valid HTTP Signature from the agent identified by `{did}`. Any other authenticated caller receives 403 Forbidden. Previously these endpoints were unauthenticated — any caller could follow or unfollow on behalf of any agent.

2. Network visibility scoping in GET /v1/units
   - Authenticated callers now only see `network`-visibility units from authors they actually follow, matching the semantics already enforced by `GET /v1/units/{id}`. Previously any authenticated caller could read all network units regardless of follow relationship.
   - Implementation: the list handler calls `list_following(caller_did)` and passes the result as `UnitFilter::network_for_authors`; both storage backends enforce the constraint efficiently (in-process filter for MemoryStorage, SQL `AND (visibility != 'network' OR author IN (…))` for SqliteStorage).

3. Peer reputation update mechanism (`PATCH /v1/peers/{node_id}`)
   - New endpoint accepts `{ "reputation": 0.0–1.0 }` and returns the updated `PeerInfo`. Returns 400 for out-of-range values, 404 for unknown peers.
   - New `Storage::update_peer_reputation` method implemented in both MemoryStorage and SqliteStorage.
   - New `ReputationUpdate` type added to `semanticweft-node-api`.

All 225 tests pass (0 failures, 0 ignored).

author: nicolasrouquette
body:
## Summary

Bridge `Parser.Stream` to `Std.Data.Iterators` and replace fuel-based fold combinators with well-founded recursion.

## Motivation

The `partial def` fold combinators (`efoldlPAux`, `foldr`, `takeUntil`, `dropUntil`, `countUntil`) block downstream verification. This PR makes them total using `Parser.Stream.remaining` as a well-founded measure, and provides a `Std.Iterators` bridge so that parser streams can be consumed with standard `for` loops.

## Changes

### `Parser/Stream.lean`
- **`LawfulParserStream`** typeclass: requires a proof that `remaining` strictly decreases on each `next?` yielding `some`:
  ```lean
  class LawfulParserStream (σ : Type _) (τ : outParam (Type _)) [Parser.Stream σ τ] : Prop where
    remaining_decreases : ∀ (s : σ) (tok : τ) (s' : σ),
      Stream.next? s = some (tok, s') → remaining s' < remaining s
  ```
- Instances proven for `Subarray τ` and `OfList τ`
- Instances with `sorry` for `String.Slice`, `Substring.Raw`, `ByteSlice` (need deeper stdlib simp lemmas for byte-index arithmetic)

### `Parser/Iterators.lean` (new)
- `StreamIterator σ τ` wrapper presenting a `Parser.Stream` as an `IterM` state
- `Iterator` instance for all `Parser.Stream` types (no `LawfulParserStream` required)
- `Finite` instance via `streamFinitenessRelation` (requires `LawfulParserStream`)
- `IteratorLoop` instance enabling `for tok in iter do ...` loops (requires `LawfulParserStream`)

### `Parser/Parser.lean`
- `efoldlPAux`: removed `fuel : Nat` parameter, now uses `termination_by Stream.remaining s` with a runtime guard

### `Parser/Basic.lean`
- `foldr`, `takeUntil`, `dropUntil`, `countUntil`: replaced fuel parameter with well-founded recursion via `termination_by Stream.remaining s₀`

## Status

- 5 files changed, +308/−33 lines
- Builds cleanly on Lean v4.28.0 (only `sorry` warnings from 3 `LawfulParserStream` instances)
- The 3 remaining `sorry` proofs need `simp` lemmas for `String.Slice`, `Substring.Raw`, and `ByteSlice` byte-index arithmetic that may not yet be available in stdlib/Batteries

## Discussion

This approach splits the concern:
- **`Parser.Stream`** — any stream with `remaining` (unchanged API contract)
- **`LawfulParserStream`** — streams that *prove* `remaining` decreases (opt-in, enables totality)
- **`mkDefault`** — remains `partial` (no `LawfulParserStream` instance), does not break existing users

The `Std.Iterators` bridge is additive — existing code is unaffected. Downstream projects that need verified folds can depend on `LawfulParserStream` instances for their concrete stream types.

## PER-69: Configure OAuth scopes including agent-specific app:assignable and app:mentionable

The required OAuth configuration was already implemented as part of PR #1 (PER-63). This PR formally tracks PER-69 by adding inline documentation to clarify the purpose of each scope.

### Scopes configured in `OAUTH_SCOPES`

| Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `read` | Default read access |
| `write` | Create/update issues and **comments** (covers Manus leaving/editing comments) |
| `app:assignable` | App can be set as delegate on issues and added to projects |
| `app:mentionable` | App can be mentioned in issues, documents, and editor surfaces |

### actor=app

The `actor: 'app'` parameter is set in the authorize URL params, switching from user-actor to app-actor mode.

### Delegate vs Assignee

When a user assigns an issue to the Manus app, Linear stores it in the `delegate` field (not `assignee`) to preserve human ownership while the agent acts on their behalf. This behaviour is now documented in the code.

author: copilot
body:
`is_facebook_post_from_today()` was calling `article.inner_text()` internally, then the scraper called it again immediately after — two cross-process Playwright DOM calls per post when only one is needed.

## Changes

- **`utils.py`**: Added optional `article_text` parameter to `is_facebook_post_from_today()`; when supplied, skips the internal `inner_text()` call
- **`leons.py` / `bigdeal.py`**: Fetch `article.inner_text()` once per post into `text_content`, validate it, then pass it via `article_text=text_content` to the date-check helper

```python
# Before: two inner_text() calls per post
if not is_facebook_post_from_today(article, self.logger):  # calls inner_text() internally
    continue
text_content = article.inner_text()  # called again

# After: one inner_text() call per post
text_content = article.inner_text()
if not is_facebook_post_from_today(article, self.logger, article_text=text_content):
    continue
```

- **`tests/test_utils.py`**: Added `test_pre_fetched_text_is_used_without_calling_inner_text` to assert `inner_text()` is never invoked on the article mock when `article_text` is provided

author: njlane314
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a reusable, header-only calibrator for raw CNN logits supporting none/Platt/isotonic methods and easy integration into ROOT-based analyses.
- Enable conversion between posterior/LLR and target priors and allow fitting from in-memory arrays or `TTree`/`TChain` expressions without requiring a ROOT dictionary.

### Description
- Add `framework/modules/ana/include/LogitCalibrator.hh` implementing `heron::LogitCalibrator` with methods `kNone`, `kPlatt`, and `kIsotonic` and a Doxygen brief.
- Expose evaluation APIs: `prob`, `log_odds`, `llr`, `posterior`, and `log_odds_target` for fit-prior and target-prior usage.
- Implement fitting routines: `fit_platt` (weighted Newton + backtracking with optional L2) and `fit_isotonic` (PAV block merging), plus overloads that read expressions via `TTreeFormula` (`fit_platt`/`fit_isotonic` from `TTree`).
- Add ROOT persistence helpers `save_to_root` / `load_from_root` that serialize parameters with `TParameter` and `TVectorD` so no class dictionary is required.
- Include robust numeric helpers and validations: stable `sigmoid`, clamping (`clamp_prob_01`/`clamp_prob`), `prior_log_odds`/`logit`, isotonic bin lookup, input checks, and weighted `pi_fit` computation.

### Testing
- Attempted to build with `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build -j2`, which failed because the repository has no `CMakeLists.txt` (command reported an error). (failed)
- Attempted `make -j2`, which failed in this environment because ROOT is not available on `PATH` (`root-config` missing), so no compiled validation ran. (failed)

author: copilot
body:
CI runs on every push/PR with no cancellation, no caching, and a redundant `pre-commit` step that re-executes tools already run explicitly — wasting minutes on stale runs, doc-only changes, and duplicate work.

## Changes

- **Concurrency**: added `cancel-in-progress: true` grouped by workflow + PR number/ref — stale runs on rapid pushes are immediately cancelled
- **`paths-ignore`**: docs (`**.md`, `docs/**`, `.gitignore`) skip CI entirely on both `push` and `pull_request`
- **Pip cache**: added `cache: "pip"` to `setup-python` — saves ~45–60 s per run after the first warm cache
- **Removed `pre-commit` step**: it re-ran `ruff format` + `ruff check`, both already explicit earlier in the job; current `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no hooks beyond ruff

## Trade-offs

| Change | Risk |
|---|---|
| `pre-commit` removed | Only ruff hooks exist today; if new hooks are added to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, they won't run in CI unless explicitly added |
| `paths-ignore` | Doc-only PRs will show no CI check; branch-protection rules should treat this as passing-by-omission |
| `cancel-in-progress` | In-flight runs are cancelled on new push — expected behaviour, latest commit always gets a fresh run |

body:
## Summary
This PR adds a comprehensive test suite for all scrapers and improves the robustness of the scraping infrastructure by introducing safe JSON parsing, better error handling, and data validation.

## Key Changes

### Test Coverage
- **New test files** for all scrapers:
  - `tests/test_base.py`: Tests for `BaseScraper` including `_safe_json()` and `search_all_pages()` with pagination, error handling, deduplication, and validation
  - `tests/test_instagram.py`: Instagram scraper tests covering API responses and edge cases
  - `tests/test_line.py`: LINE scraper tests for HTML parsing and contact extraction
  - `tests/test_tabelog.py`: Tabelog scraper tests for restaurant data parsing
  - `tests/test_itown.py`: itown scraper tests for shop information extraction
  - `tests/test_gurunavi.py`: Gurunavi API scraper tests

### Core Infrastructure Improvements
- **Added `_safe_json()` method** to `BaseScraper`: Safely parses JSON responses with proper error logging, returning empty dict on failure instead of raising exceptions
- **Enhanced `search_all_pages()`** with:
  - Deduplication by `source_id` to prevent duplicate results across pages
  - Consecutive error tracking (stops after 2 consecutive errors)
  - Validation to skip records with empty `store_name`
  - Fallback to `store_name` when `source_id` is empty
- **Updated all scrapers** to use `_safe_json()` instead of direct `response.json()` calls:
  - Instagram, Gurunavi, HotPepper, Google Places scrapers

### Data Quality Improvements
- **Improved email regex patterns** in LINE and Tabelog scrapers to use word boundaries (`\b`) and stricter validation, preventing false positives from CSS selectors
- **Enhanced filtering logic** in itown and HotPepper scrapers to accept records with address-only information (not just phone/email)
- **Better contact validation** in `search_all_pages()` to handle edge cases

### UI Enhancements (app.py)
- Added quality badge display showing information completeness (充実/標準/最低限)
- Added search history feature with localStorage persistence (max 5 recent searches)
- Improved error reporting in results summary with detailed error messages
- Enhanced status messages to show per-source error details when no results found

## Notable Implementation Details
- Email regex now uses `\b[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]*@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9.-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}\b` pattern to avoid matching invalid formats
- Deduplication in `search_all_pages()` uses a set to track seen `source_id` values, keeping first occurrence
- Error handling is graceful: single page errors don't stop pagination, but consecutive errors do
- All tests use mocking to avoid external API calls and ensure reliability

body:
### Motivation
- The import job was raising `MultipleObjectsReturned` when `Set.objects.update_or_create(tcgdex_id=...)` encountered multiple DB rows with the same `tcgdex_id`, causing Celery retries and task failures.
- The intent is to make imports resilient to existing duplicate rows and to prevent new duplicates at the schema level.

### Description
- Make `import_sets_from_tcgdex` defensive by querying `Set.objects.filter(tcgdex_id=...)`, keeping the first row, deleting other duplicates, updating the keeper with the new data, and falling back to `Set.objects.create(...)` when none exists.
- Add a conditional unique constraint on `Set.tcgdex_id` (ignoring `NULL` and empty string) in `Set.Meta` to prevent future duplicates (`cards_set_unique_non_blank_tcgdex_id`).
- Add data migration `0019_dedupe_set_tcgdex_id_and_constraint.py` that deduplicates existing `Set` rows by `tcgdex_id` (merging basic fields onto the keeper) and then adds the unique constraint.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall backend/cards/services/import_sets.py backend/cards/models.py backend/cards/migrations/0019_dedupe_set_tcgdex_id_and_constraint.py`, which completed successfully.

author: edwiniac
body:
## Problem

When using `extra_headers: {anthropic-beta: context-1m-2025-08-07}` with `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6`, the header is filtered out and Claude's 1M context window feature is unavailable.

Users get: `prompt is too long: 460500 tokens > 200000 maximum`

## Root Cause

In `anthropic_beta_headers_config.json`, the `context-1m-2025-08-07` header is set to `null` for vertex_ai, causing it to be filtered out by `filter_and_transform_beta_headers()`.

Other providers (anthropic, azure_ai, bedrock, databricks) correctly have this set to `"context-1m-2025-08-07"`.

## Fix

Set `context-1m-2025-08-07` to `"context-1m-2025-08-07"` for vertex_ai provider.

## Changes

- `litellm/anthropic_beta_headers_config.json`: Changed `context-1m-2025-08-07` from `null` to `"context-1m-2025-08-07"` for vertex_ai

Fixes #21861

## Summary
- 6 jobs per PR run → 2. Full 3×Python matrix kept only on `main` push. Stale runs cancelled automatically.

## Rationale
- **`concurrency` + `cancel-in-progress: true`** — kills superseded runs on force-push/rebase; ~20–40% saving from wasted runs alone.
- **Lint matrix 3× → 1× (Python 3.10)** — `mypy` is pinned to `python_version = "3.10"`; ruff/black results are version-agnostic. Zero signal lost.
- **Removed `pre-commit run --all-files` step** — ruff, black, and mypy already run individually in prior steps; pre-commit was a full duplicate pass.
- **Test matrix on PRs: 3× → 1× (3.10)** — full `["3.10","3.11","3.12"]` matrix preserved on every push to `main`, so cross-version regressions are still caught before deployment.
- **`paths-ignore: docs/**`, `**/*.md`** — doc-only changes skip all CI entirely.
- **`permissions: contents: read`** — locks down `GITHUB_TOKEN` to minimum required scope (fixes CodeQL `missing-workflow-permissions` alert).
- **Dependabot**: minor/patch GitHub Actions bumps grouped into one PR; `open-pull-requests-limit` 10 → 5 for both ecosystems.

**Before/after job count:**

| Event | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| PR push | 6 jobs | 2 jobs |
| Push to `main` | 6 jobs | 4 jobs |

**Trade-offs:** 3.11/3.12 test failures only surface after merge to `main`, not during PR review. Risk is low given the project's stdlib-heavy dependency profile.

## LLM involvement
- Files modified by LLM: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`

## Problem `package_skill.py` includes `.git/` internals (and other VCS/build artifacts) in `.skill` archives. This causes: - Unnecessary archive bloat - Git history and metadata leakage in distributable skill packages - Poor artifact hygiene ## Fix Add an exclusion set checked during the `rglob` walk that skips: - `.git`, `.svn`, `.hg` (VCS directories) - `__pycache__` (Python bytecode cache) - `node_modules` (JS dependencies) - `.DS_Store` (macOS metadata) The check uses path parts matching so nested occurrences are also excluded (e.g. `subdir/.git/objects`). ## Changes - `skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py`: Add `EXCLUDED_DIRS` set and skip matching paths Fixes #23149

The implementation uses path part matching to filter out any file or directory containing excluded names in its path.

author: rmichelena
body:
## Problema raíz

El `execute()` del nodo tenía dos enfoques mezclados e incompatibles:
- La UI se genera desde el OpenAPI spec vía `@devlikeapro/n8n-openapi-node` (que produce propiedades con routing declarativo)
- Pero el `execute()` reimplementaba manualmente el routing, la URL, los parámetros y la autenticación OAuth2

Esto causaba que prácticamente todas las operaciones fallaran de distintas formas.

## Cambios incluidos

### Fixes de parámetros (commits iniciales)
- **Query params ignorados**: `getNodeParameter('queryParameters', i, {})` buscaba un objeto agregado que no existe. El builder genera campos individuales (`filter`, `start`, `limit`, `sort`) con `routing.send.type: 'query'`. Fix: iterar `properties` por tipo de routing.
- **Body params ignorados**: mismo problema con `getNodeParameter('requestBody', i, {})`. Fix: mismo patrón para `routing.send.type: 'body'`.
- **Double slash en URL**: el `OperationParser` produce valores como `"GET /Assistance/Ticket"` (con slash), al hacer `'/' + pathPart` resultaba `//Assistance/Ticket`.
- **Valores vacíos default contaminando body**: campos no completados llegaban como `"{}"`, `"[]"`, `"[\n  {}\n]"`. Fix: helper `isEmptyValue()` que maneja strings serializados por n8n.

### Refactor principal: `execute()` con `httpRequestWithAuthentication`
Reemplaza ~200 líneas de gestión manual de OAuth2 + construcción de requests por el helper estándar de n8n. Esto resuelve en un solo commit:
- Token OAuth2 serializado como JSON en vez de `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
- Token solicitado una vez por item en lugar de cachearse (con 50 items → 100 requests)
- `ignoreSSLIssues` de las credenciales completamente ignorado
- `clientId`/`clientSecret` enviados como Basic Auth incondicionalmente
- Trailing slash en `glpiUrl` producía `//api.php/...`
- Headers GLPI (`GLPI-Entity`, `Accept-Language`, etc.) hardcodeados con nombres que el builder no genera — nunca se enviaban; ahora se leen por `routing.send.type: 'header'`
- Método HTTP sin validación → ahora falla con error claro
- Path params no resueltos (`{id}`) silenciosos → ahora `NodeOperationError` descriptivo
- Regex de path params con `lastIndex` inestable → reemplazada por `replace+callback`

### Fixes de calidad
- `val === 0` tratado como vacío bloqueaba valores legítimos (`entity=0` = entidad raíz, `start=0` para paginación)
- `catch {}` genérico tragaba errores reales de expresiones — ahora re-throw de `NodeOperationError`
- `requestDefaults` (baseURL + headers) eliminado: no tiene efecto con `execute()` personalizado, su presencia era engañosa
- Dependencia `@devlikeapro/n8n-openapi-node` pineada a `0.1.4` exacto (pre-1.0 con `^` permite breaking changes en minor versions)

### Housekeeping
- `Glpi.node.json`: URL de documentación apuntaba a la API legacy REST (GLPI 9/10) — corregida a la HL API de GLPI 11
- `openapi-v11.json`: archivo idéntico a `openapi.json` (4.6 MB duplicados) eliminado
- CI: escuchaba en branch `main` que no existe — corregido a `master`

body:
## What's Changed

### Features

- **Fill observability and signal propagation**: Added comprehensive observability for `fillForm()` operations with signal propagation to `generateText()` for proper cancellation, extended `onLlmCallEnd` callbacks with duration and provider metadata, LLM call details in timeline entries, structured error classification (`errorType`/`errorCode`), and raw event logs for debugging (#158)
- **FillRecord source-of-truth enrichment**: Transform FillRecord into comprehensive source of record with provenance tracking (markform version, input hash, schema version), effective config snapshot, per-turn enrichment (form progress, rejection details, issue refs), and opt-in raw patches via `--record-patches` flag (#161)
- **External retry control**: Expose `maxRetries` in `FillOptions` to allow production harnesses to disable hidden AI SDK retries and manage retries externally with full observability (#162)
- **Table row validation improvements**: Drop fully-empty table rows during normalization, warn on sparse rows (>50% empty cells), strengthen `minRows` validation, and add defensive handling of unknown cell states (#161, #163)

### Fixes

- Fixed signal propagation bug where `FillOptions.signal` wasn't reaching `generateText()`, preventing cancellation of in-flight LLM calls (#158)
- Fixed `onLlmCallEnd` callback to fire on failure (timeout, rate limit, network error), not just success, eliminating orphaned pending call entries (#158)
- Fixed `isRowFullyEmpty()` to defensively treat unknown/malformed cell states as NOT empty, avoiding accidental data loss (#163)
- Fixed aborted table row handling to preserve aborted cells since they carry intentional agent signal (#161)

### Refactoring

- Extracted shared `isCellEmpty()` helper to eliminate duplication between row normalization and validation (#163)

### Motivation
- Avoid panics from entropy failures in env secret generation and make failures observable to callers. 
- Surface and wrap low-level entropy read errors so CLI flows can fail fast with actionable context. 
- Provide a test seam to simulate entropy read failures and ensure failure paths are exercised. 

### Description
- Added an `entropyRead` seam and changed `randomSecret` and `randomSuffix` to return `(string, error)` and report entropy read errors instead of panicking. 
- Updated `generateEnvValues` to return `(generated, newlyGenerated, error)` and wrap generator failures with key-specific context using `%w`. 
- Threaded and wrapped the new error through CLI callers (`runEnvInit` now returns generation errors; `runQuickstart` reports a wrapped Env init failure) while preserving existing success-path console output. 
- Updated tests to the new signatures and added two unit tests that force entropy-read failures via the `entropyRead` seam to verify error propagation. 
- Updated `PLAN.md` and `TASKS.md` to reflect the work and recorded test results.

author: lailoo
body:
## Summary - **Bug**: Internal reminder guardrail note leaks into user-visible Telegram/channel messages - **Root cause**: `appendUnscheduledReminderNote()` in `agent-runner.ts` appends the note directly to `payload.text`, which flows to channel delivery - **Fix**: Move the note to a new `systemNote` field on `ReplyPayload` that channels don't render Fixes #23124 ## Problem When the agent makes a reminder commitment (e.g. "I'll remind you tomorrow morning") but doesn't actually schedule a cron job, the system appends an internal guardrail note: > Note: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically. This note was appended directly to `payload.text` in `appendUnscheduledReminderNote()` at `agent-runner.ts:87-90`. Since all channel delivery code (Telegram, Slack, Discord, etc.) reads `payload.text` to send messages, the note was visible to end users. **Before fix:** Input: Agent says "I'll remind you tomorrow morning." (no cron.add) Output: "I'll remind you tomorrow morning.\n\nNote: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically." ## Changes - `src/auto-reply/types.ts` — Add `systemNote?: string` field to `ReplyPayload` for internal annotations - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — Set `systemNote` instead of modifying `text` in `appendUnscheduledReminderNote()` - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — Update existing test + add regression test **After fix:** Input: Agent says "I'll remind you tomorrow morning." (no cron.add) Output text: "I'll remind you tomorrow morning." Output systemNote: "Note: I did not schedule a reminder in this turn, so this will not trigger automatically." ## Test plan - [x] Updated test: guard note now asserts `systemNote` field instead of `text` concatenation - [x] New test: "does not leak guard note into visible text" — explicitly verifies `text` does not contain the note - [x] All 21 existing tests in `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` pass - [x] All 36 tests in `agent-runner.runreplyagent.test.ts` pass - [x] Format check passes (`pnpm format:check`) ## Effect on User Experience **Before:** Users see an internal system note ("Note: I did not schedule a reminder...") appended to the agent's message in Telegram and other channels. **After:** The agent's message is clean. The guardrail note is preserved internally in `systemNote` for diagnostics but never shown to users.

Greptile Summary

Clean, focused bugfix that moves the unscheduled-reminder guardrail note from `payload.text` (visible to users in all channels) to a new `systemNote` field on `ReplyPayload` that no channel adapter reads. - **`src/auto-reply/types.ts`**: Adds `systemNote?: string` to `ReplyPayload` with clear JSDoc annotation - **`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`**: `appendUnscheduledReminderNote()` now sets `systemNote` instead of concatenating to `text`, also removing the `trimEnd()` call that is no longer needed - **Tests**: Updated existing assertion to check `systemNote` instead of `text` concatenation, plus a new regression test explicitly verifying the note does not appear in `text` - **`CHANGELOG.md`**: Entry added under Fixes The fix is safe because all channel delivery paths (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, WhatsApp, iMessage) only read `text`, `mediaUrl`/`mediaUrls`, and `channelData` from payloads — none read `systemNote`. The `normalizeReplyPayloadsForDelivery` function does carry `systemNote` through via spread, but downstream channel adapters destructure only the fields they need.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it's a minimal, well-tested fix that moves an internal note out of user-visible text. - The change is small and surgical (3 lines of logic changed). All channel delivery paths were verified to only read `text`/`mediaUrl`/`mediaUrls`/`channelData` — none read `systemNote`. Tests cover both the positive case (note goes into `systemNote`) and the negative regression case (note does not appear in `text`). No new risk is introduced. - No files require special attention. body:
## Summary
Completely rebuilt the application from a simple message board into a sophisticated ML job crawler with real-time progress tracking and optional LangGraph-powered advanced analysis mode.

## Key Changes

**Frontend (public/index.html)**
- Redesigned UI with dark theme and modern styling (GitHub-inspired color scheme)
- Added mode toggle between "Basic Mode" and "Advanced Mode (LangGraph)"
- Implemented real-time progress tracking with SSE-based log streaming
- Created job card display with filtering by source, relevance scoring, and ML subfield tagging
- Added responsive controls for API key input and model selection (advanced mode only)
- Integrated visual feedback with status badges, spinner animations, and score visualization

**Backend (server.js)**
- Replaced message board API with ML job crawler endpoints
- Implemented three job sources: RemoteOK, We Work Remotely, and Hacker News
- Added session-based crawl management with in-memory storage
- **Basic mode**: Parallel scraping from multiple sources with deduplication
- **Advanced mode**: LangGraph workflow with multi-step pipeline:
  - Search query planning via LLM
  - Source crawling and aggregation
  - LLM-based job enrichment with relevance scoring (1-10), ML subfield classification, and seniority level detection
  - Market summary generation
- Implemented SSE endpoint for real-time progress streaming
- Added job retrieval endpoint with session isolation

**Dependencies (package.json)**
- Replaced single `express` dependency with: `axios` (HTTP requests), `cheerio` (HTML parsing), `@langchain/langgraph`, and `@langchain/openai` (for advanced mode)

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Deduplication**: Jobs tracked by unique IDs across sources to prevent duplicates
- **Error handling**: Graceful fallbacks when LLM parsing fails; basic crawl continues even if individual sources fail
- **Real-time UX**: SSE streaming provides live progress updates without polling
- **LLM integration**: Configurable model selection (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo) with temperature=0 for consistent scoring
- **Job enrichment**: LLM scores jobs 1-10 for ML relevance, categorizes by subfield (NLP, CV, MLOps, etc.), and identifies seniority level
- **Responsive design**: Mobile-friendly layout with collapsible advanced settings and scrollable log viewer

author: achan-bot
body:
## Summary

- `bin/deploy` sent SIGTERM to Puma but never waited for it to actually exit. With Solid Queue running inside Puma (`SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA=1`), graceful shutdown takes time to drain workers. The deploy script would finish immediately while Puma was still alive, so `bin/prod`'s restart loop never triggered — requiring a manual kill and restart to pick up new code.
- Now waits up to 30s for the process to exit after SIGTERM, falls back to SIGKILL, and cleans up the PID file. Each step is logged to `log/deploy.log` for debugging.

## Test plan

- [ ] Push a change to `main` to trigger a webhook deploy
- [ ] Check `log/deploy.log` to confirm the server stop timing is logged
- [ ] Verify the site picks up the new code without manually restarting `bin/prod`

Add 1,310 new recipes by processing the full pending generation queue
across homebrew (1,125), crates.io (102), and rubygems (83). Backfill
satisfies metadata on 21 existing library recipes to enable ecosystem
name resolution. Create 10 new library recipes for priority blockers

---

## What This Accomplishes

The recipe queue held 5,275 entries across all ecosystems, with 2,830
still pending. This PR processes every pending entry: those that produce
a valid recipe are added to the registry, and those that fail (library
bottles without CLI binaries, tap formulas not in homebrew core, packages
without executables) are marked as failed in the queue.

|-----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Homebrew | 2,645 | 1,125 | 1,520 |
| crates.io | 102 | 102 | 0 |

body:
This PR replaces single split `(train → validation)` model selection with true walk-forward validation using 156-era chunks and 8-era purge, then uses only walk-forward CORR outcomes to choose `recommended_num_iteration` for final ensemble training.

- **Walk-forward framework (156/8)**
  - Added `src/walkforward.py` with `WFWindow` and `build_windows(...)` to generate Numerai-style windows:
    - train up to `val_start - purge - 1`
    - purge `[train_end+1, val_start-1]`
    - validate on each 156-era chunk for `k >= 2`
  - Supports non-perfectly contiguous era coverage by requiring train/val presence per window.

- **Robust era normalization**
  - Added `src/era_utils.py` with `era_to_int(...)` for consistent era parsing from ints or strings like `era123`.
  - Standardized era handling for all walk-forward indexing.

- **Chronological combined training corpus**
  - Extended `LoadedData` to include `x_all/y_all/era_all/era_all_int`.
  - `load_train_valid_frames()` now concatenates train+validation and applies stable sort by era integer for chronological walk-forward splits.

- **Walk-forward evaluation + recommendation**
  - Added `evaluate_walkforward(...)` in `src/train_colab.py`:
    - builds windows from combined era history
    - optionally keeps last `N` windows (`walkforward_max_windows`)
    - trains only one tuning seed (`walkforward_tune_seed`) for compute control
    - computes per-window `best_iter` via CORR scan and per-window mean per-era Numerai CORR
  - Logs:
    - `walkforward/windows` W&B table (window ranges + metrics)
    - summary scalars: mean CORR, std CORR, sharpe, hit-rate
  - Produces `recommended_num_iteration = median(best_iter_per_window)`.

- **Final training flow switched to walk-forward signal**
  - When `walkforward_enabled=True`, each ensemble seed is trained once on **all historical data** (`x_all/y_all`) using fixed `recommended_num_iteration`.
  - Added `fit_lgbm_final(...)` helper for fixed-iteration final fit (no early-stopping dependency for selection).

- **Checkpoint / manifest schema updates**
  - Checkpoint now records top-level `walkforward` settings + recommended iteration and validates compatibility on resume.
  - Manifest now includes walk-forward summary metadata.
  - Artifact now includes `walkforward_windows.json` with per-window records.

- **Config knobs (env-backed)**
  - Added:
    - `walkforward_enabled` (default `True`)
    - `walkforward_chunk_size` (default `156`)
    - `walkforward_purge_eras` (default `8`)
    - `walkforward_max_windows` (default `4`)
    - `walkforward_tune_seed` (default first ensemble seed)
    - `walkforward_log_models` (default `False`)

- **Focused utility coverage**
  - Added `tests/test_walkforward_utils.py` for:
    - era parsing correctness
    - canonical window boundaries (e.g., `1–148 / 149–156 / 157–312`).

Example of the new window contract:

```python
from walkforward import build_windows
import numpy as np

eras = np.arange(1, 625, dtype=np.int32)
windows = build_windows(eras, chunk_size=156, purge_eras=8, min_chunk_index=2)

# first window:
# train 1..148, purge 149..156, validate 157..312
print(windows[0])
```

body:
No native telemetry exists in the Claude Code marketplace, making it impossible to measure ado-flow plugin adoption. This adds passive, zero-friction telemetry by stamping ADO resources with command-scoped markers whenever the plugin writes to them — queryable via WIQL, build tag filters, or PR label searches within the ADO org.

## Approach

Each write-path command appends a distinct tag to the resource it modifies. All telemetry calls are **silent and fire-and-forget** (`2>/dev/null || true`) — failures never surface to the user.

| Command | Resource | Marker |
|---|---|---|
| `adoflow:workitems` | Work item (create) | `System.Tags = adoflow:workitems` |
| `adoflow:prs` | PR (create) | Label `adoflow:prs` via REST |
| `adoflow:pipelines` | Build (trigger) | Build tag `adoflow:pipelines` |
| `adoflow:sprint-update` | Work items (update) | `System.Tags` appended with `adoflow:sprint-update` |
| `adoflow:link-prs` | PR (after linking) | Label `adoflow:link-prs` via REST |

Read-only commands (`standup`, `morning`) have no telemetry — nothing to stamp.

## Key implementation details

**Work item creation** — straightforward, new items have no existing tags:
```bash
az boards work-item create ... --fields "System.Tags=adoflow:workitems"
```

**Sprint-update** — work items already have tags; Phase 2c parse.js now computes `mergedTags` per item using an exact boundary check (split on `; `, not `includes()`) to prevent false dedup against similarly-named tags. Phase 5 passes the merged value via `--fields`:
```bash
az boards work-item update ... --fields "System.Tags={MERGED_TAGS_FOR_ID}"
```

**PR labels** — uses the ADO REST labels endpoint, which creates the label if it doesn't exist:
```bash
az rest --method post \
  --url "https://dev.azure.com/{ORG}/{PR_PROJECT}/_apis/git/repositories/{REPO}/pullRequests/{PR_ID}/labels?api-version=7.1" \
  --headers "Content-Type=application/json" \
  --body '{"name":"adoflow:prs"}' \
  -o json 2>/dev/null || true
```

body:
Closes #55

## Summary

- Create `SimpleEPGP/UI/Utils.lua` with 6 shared utility functions and 1 constant that replace ~200+ lines of duplicate boilerplate across all 9 UI files
- Refactor all 9 UI consumers (Config, OfficerPanel, Standings, Leaderboard, StandbyManager, GPConfig, ExportFrame, LootPopup, AwardFrame) to delegate to Utils
- Update `.toc` to load `UI\Utils.lua` before all other UI files
- Update all 9 test files to load Utils.lua before consumer UI modules

### Extracted utilities

| Function | Replaces |
|----------|----------|
| `Utils.DIALOG_BACKDROP` | Identical backdrop table in 7 files |
| `Utils.CreateStandardFrame(opts)` | 30-40 line frame creation boilerplate in every UI file (movable, draggable, backdrop, title, close button, Escape-to-close, UISpecialFrames) |
| `Utils.CreateSectionHeader(parent, text, x, y)` | Gold section headers in Config.lua and OfficerPanel.lua |
| `Utils.CreateLabel(parent, text, x, y)` | White labels in Config.lua and OfficerPanel.lua |
| `Utils.CreateEditBox(parent, x, y, width, maxLetters)` | EditBox creation in Config.lua and OfficerPanel.lua |
| `Utils.CreateScrollbar(opts)` | 20-line scrollbar creation in 6 files |
| `Utils.EnableMouseWheelScroll(frame, scrollBar, step)` | Mouse wheel handler in 6 files |

### Design decisions

- `CreateStandardFrame` accepts an `opts` table with sensible defaults but allows overrides for `backdrop`, `backdropColor`, `strata`, `point`, `titleFont`, and `onClose` -- this covers all variations across the 9 consumers
- Config.lua retains a local `CreateEditBox` wrapper that adds `dbKey`/`widgets` tracking on top of `Utils.CreateEditBox`
- ExportFrame repositions its scrollbar after creation (non-standard -12 x-offset) via `ClearAllPoints` + re-anchoring
- Net change: **366 insertions, 476 deletions** (-110 lines)

## Validation

- `luacheck SimpleEPGP/ --config .luacheckrc` -- 0 warnings / 0 errors across all 18 files
- `busted test/` -- sandbox environment blocked test execution; manual verification needed

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `busted test/` locally to verify all 731 tests pass

- [ ] Verify in-game: `/sepgp standings` opens Standings panel correctly
- [ ] Verify in-game: `/sepgp leaderboard` opens Leaderboard panel correctly
- [ ] Verify frames are draggable, Escape-to-close works, close button works

author: chenders
body:
## Summary

- Split multi-word actor name searches into independent ILIKE conditions so each word matches anywhere in the name
- Searching "paul smith" now finds "Paul L. Smith" (previously required exact contiguous match)
- Applied consistently across all 6 search locations: bio enrichment, biographies, coverage, death details, all deaths, and death watch

## Details

The root cause was `ILIKE '%paul smith%'` requiring the search terms to appear as a contiguous substring. Actors with middle names/initials (Paul L. Smith), suffixes (Robert Downey Jr.), or alternate name formats would not match.

The fix splits on whitespace and generates one ILIKE per word:
```sql
-- Before: misses 'Paul L. Smith'
WHERE name ILIKE '%paul smith%'

-- After: matches any name containing both words
WHERE name ILIKE '%paul%' AND name ILIKE '%smith%'
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 77 existing tests pass across 3 test files
- [x] TypeScript type-check passes
- [x] Verified against production DB: "paul smith" returns Paul L. Smith (id 25991)
- [x] Single-word searches still work identically

author: alejandrogispert
body:
# Case-Insensitive Username Login, Closes #3981



**Author:** Alejandro Gispert  
**First-time contributor to Umami**

---



```markdown

### What

Makes login case-insensitive: `Admin`, `admin`, and `ADMIN` all resolve to the same account.

### Why

- Reduces friction when users don't recall exact casing
- Aligns with common expectations from modern apps
- Avoids lockouts caused by caps lock

### How

- Usernames are normalized to lowercase on create, update, and lookup
- Run the provided SQL to lowercase existing usernames in the database

### Changes

- `src/queries/prisma/user.ts` – `getUserByUsername()` lowercases before lookup
- `src/app/api/users/route.ts` – Store and check usernames in lowercase on create
- `src/app/api/users/[userId]/route.ts` – Store lowercase on update; fix uniqueness check

### Post-merge: run this SQL

Existing users with mixed-case usernames must be updated. Run against your database:

```sql
UPDATE "user" SET username = LOWER(username) WHERE username != LOWER(username);
```

---

## Full documentation

## Summary

This PR makes user login case-insensitive so that usernames like `Admin`, `admin`, and `ADMIN` all resolve to the same account.

---

## Problem

Login was case-sensitive: a user created with username `admin` could not log in by typing `Admin` or `ADMIN`. This led to:

- Friction for users who don't recall the exact casing
- Inconsistent behavior compared to many modern apps
- More lockouts caused by accidental caps lock

---

## Solution

Usernames are normalized to lowercase on storage and lookup:

1. **Storage** – Usernames are stored in lowercase when creating or updating users.
2. **Lookup** – User lookup always uses lowercase when resolving a username.
3. **Uniqueness** – Username uniqueness is enforced in a case-insensitive way (e.g. `Admin` and `admin` cannot coexist).

---

## Changes

### 1. `src/queries/prisma/user.ts`

- **`getUserByUsername()`** – Normalizes the input with `username.toLowerCase()` before querying, so lookups are case-insensitive.

### 2. `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts`

- No code changes; it already calls `getUserByUsername()`, which now handles case-insensitivity.

### 3. `src/app/api/users/route.ts`

- **User creation** – Uses `username.toLowerCase()` when checking for existing users and when creating new users.

### 4. `src/app/api/users/[userId]/route.ts`

- **User update** – Uses `username.toLowerCase()` when updating usernames.
- **Uniqueness check** – Fixed two issues when validating username changes:
  - **Variable shadowing:** The lookup reused the variable `user` (shadowing the current user), causing confusion. Renamed to `existingUser`.
- **Same-user case change:** Previously, if the lookup returned any user (including the current user), the update was rejected. Now we only reject when a different user already has that username. That way, a user can safely “change” their username from `Admin` to `admin` (same logical username) without being blocked.

---

## Post-merge: run this SQL

Existing users with mixed-case usernames must be updated. Run this against your database after merging:

```sql
UPDATE "user" SET username = LOWER(username) WHERE username != LOWER(username);
```

**Note:** This will fail if there are case-variant duplicates (e.g. both `Admin` and `admin`). Resolve those manually before running.

---

## Testing

- [ ] Login with uppercase, mixed case, and lowercase variants of a username.
- [ ] Create a new user and confirm it is stored in lowercase.
- [ ] Update an existing user's username and confirm it is stored in lowercase.
- [ ] Ensure username uniqueness is enforced case-insensitively (e.g. cannot create `admin` if `Admin` exists).

---

## Backward Compatibility

- **Existing users:** The migration updates stored usernames to lowercase; login continues to work.
- **Display:** Usernames are shown as stored (typically lowercase after running the SQL).
- **Breaking change:** No; behavior is additive and improves UX.

author: kpumuk
body:
<!-- Explain the changes in the pull request below: -->
  
This PR fixes a TLS hang/timeout in Ruby Thrift with `NonblockingServer` + `SSLServerSocket` + `FramedTransport` (when the client socket has a non-nil timeout).

The timed `Thrift::Socket#read` path does `IO.select` and then `readpartial`. With `OpenSSL::SSL::SSLSocket`, `readpartial` can decrypt a full TLS record but return only the requested bytes, leaving
  the rest in the SSL internal buffer. The next `IO.select` waits on the raw fd, which cannot see those buffered SSL bytes, so the framed payload read can block until timeout. This shows up especially with framed reads (4-byte frame size first, then frame body).

The solution is to switch timed `read`/`write` to ` read_nonblock` / `write_nonblock` and only call `IO.select` after `IO::WaitReadable` / `IO::WaitWritable`. This keeps timeouts intact and makes reads/writes SSL-buffer-aware. Note that we can receive `IO::WaitWritable` on reads, and `IO::WaitReadable` on writes on SSL sockets, so we need to handle both cases.

Additionally, timeout tracking now uses a monotonic clock to avoid drift or wall-clock adjustments affecting deadline checks.

### Motivation
- Make the `/ready` readiness probe fail-safe so unexpected dependency failures do not bubble up as 500s to callers or probes.
- Provide a stable OpenAPI/Pydantic schema for readiness responses so external tooling can rely on response shape.
- Ensure the DB dependency check uses a safe session lifecycle and clear return values for downstream logic.

### Description
- Add `ReadinessDependency` and `ReadinessResponse` Pydantic models and tighten status fields to `Literal["ok","error"]` / `Literal["ok","degraded"]` for stable schemas and OpenAPI generation.
- Implement `GET /ready` that reports dependency-level statuses and maps any non-`ok` dependency to a `degraded` readiness state.
- Introduce `_database_dependency_status(session_factory)` which accepts a generic session-factory callable, uses a context-managed session to run `SELECT 1`, and returns explicit `"ok"` or `"error"` literals.
- Harden dependency checks by catching `SQLAlchemyError` and any other unexpected `Exception` and treating them as dependency errors instead of letting them raise.
- Add unit tests covering the happy path, OpenAPI schema exposure for `/ready`, the degraded path when the DB helper is broken, and direct tests that the helper returns `"error"` for both `SQLAlchemyError` and unexpected runtime errors.
- Update `docs/api.md` and `docs/operations.md` to document the new `/ready` endpoint, its response shape, and the `database` check.

body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the integer literal parsing system to use `u128` and `i128` as the primary parsing types instead of `u64`, enabling proper handling of larger integer values and improving range checking for all primitive integer types.

## Key Changes

- **Unified literal parsing**: Replaced `parse_int_literal()` with `parse_u128_literal()` and `parse_i128_literal()` functions that parse directly into 128-bit types
  - `parse_u128_literal()`: Parses unsigned literals (decimal, hex, binary, octal, scientific notation)
  - `parse_i128_literal()`: Parses signed literals, delegating to unsigned parser for non-negative values
  
- **Improved range checking**: Updated `check_int_range_positive()` and `check_int_range_negative()` to accept `u128` values instead of `u64`, allowing proper validation of the full range of literal values before narrowing to target types

- **Simplified i128/u128 struct literal handling**: Consolidated duplicate logic for handling `i128` and `u128` struct type constructors
  - Unified parsing path that handles both types with a single `parse_result` match
  - Cleaner error handling with a single error case instead of separate branches per type
  - Removed `unpack_u128()` function (now only `unpack_i128()` is needed)

- **Code cleanup**:
  - Introduced `normalize_numeric_literal()` helper to centralize underscore removal and lowercasing
  - Removed `clean_literal_repr()` function in favor of direct literal representation usage
  - Simplified negated literal handling by removing unnecessary normalization calls

## Implementation Details

- All integer literal values are now parsed into their maximum representable type (u128 for unsigned, i128 for signed) before being narrowed to the target type
- This ensures accurate range validation and prevents overflow during intermediate parsing steps
- The refactoring maintains backward compatibility while improving correctness for edge cases involving large literal values

### What does it do?
Introduces `DateFormatHelper` utility that replaces deprecated `strftime()` calls. When `ext-intl` is available, it uses `IntlDateFormatter` with ICU patterns; otherwise falls back to `date()` with strftime-to-date format conversion. Replaces all `strftime()` usage in:
- `modFile` (getLastAccessed, getLastModified)
- `modOutputFilter` (strftime, date, fuzzydate filters)
- Date TV output render
- `GetInputPropertyConfigs` (date format examples)
- `modTransportProvider` (package release dates)

### Why is it needed?
`strftime()` and `gmstrftime()` are deprecated in PHP 8.1 and removed in PHP 9.0. This causes deprecation warnings and will break on future PHP versions.

### How to test
1. Run on PHP 8.1+ and verify no deprecation warnings for date formatting
2. Test Date TV output with various formats (e.g. `%A %d, %B %Y`, `%Y-%m-%d %T`)
3. Test output filters: strftime, date, fuzzydate on a resource
4. Check file manager: last accessed/modified times
5. Check Package Management: release dates display correctly

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)
Resolves #16017

## Summary
- Rewrites `egg-health-inspect` to use Claude Code headless mode (`claude --print`) instead of direct `httpx.post()` API calls
- Adds `scripts/check-model-versions.py` AST-based linter (EGG201) enforcing model alias form (`sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku` instead of `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`)
- Updates pinned model version in `ANTHROPIC_HEALTH_CHECK_MODEL` from `claude-3-haiku-20240307` to `claude-haiku-4-5`

## Context

PR #868 moved the agent inspector's LLM call from the orchestrator into the sandbox, which was the right architectural direction. However, the sandbox script still called the Anthropic API directly via `httpx.post()` with an API key, bypassing Claude Code. Additionally, it pinned `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` rather than using the alias form.

This PR enforces two invariants going forward:
1. **Single Claude pathway**: All LLM calls go through `claude --print` (Claude Code headless), never through direct API calls. The rewritten `egg-health-inspect` uses `subprocess.run(["claude", "--print", ...])` with `--max-turns 1`.
2. **Model aliases only**: Code must use short aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) rather than full model identifiers (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`). A new AST-based linter detects violations with `# noqa: EGG201` suppression for legitimate exceptions (docstring examples, raw API health checks).

Both linters are wired into `.github/workflows/lint.yml`. All 174 tests pass (27 new + 24 + 54 + 69 existing).

body:
## Summary

- **Wake button non-functional in pop-out hub**: The `SleepingAgent` component relies on `useProjectStore` to resolve the project path for the wake-up flow. The pop-out window never called `loadProjects()`, so the project store was empty and `handleWake()` silently returned early. Fixed by loading the project store during `PopoutHubView` initialization.

- **Agent state not syncing when woken from another view**: When an agent was woken from the main window, the pop-out hub's Zustand store wasn't updated because hook events from the agent CLI may not arrive promptly (the agent may sit idle at a prompt). Fixed by adding a PTY data listener in `useAgentStateSync` that detects when a sleeping agent's PTY starts producing output and transitions it to `running`. Uses a `Set` for O(1) dedup so subsequent data events are no-ops, and resets tracking on PTY exit.

## Changes

- `PopoutHubView.tsx`: Import `useProjectStore`, call `loadProjects()` during `loadHubData()`
- `PopoutWindow.tsx`: Add PTY `onData` listener in `useAgentStateSync` to detect sleeping→running transitions
- `PopoutWindow.test.tsx`: Tests for PTY data subscription, sleeping→running transition, dedup behavior, and exit reset
- `PopoutHubView.test.tsx`: Test that project store is loaded during initialization

## Test plan

- [x] All 3143 unit tests pass
- [x] TypeScript typecheck passes
- [x] Build (`npm run make`) succeeds

author: trustin
body:
## Motivation

The markdown editor had several usability problems that degraded the writing experience:

1. **Editor resize**: Dragging the resize handle could only set a minimum height, so the editor would grow past the user-set size as content was added. There was no way to pin the editor to a fixed viewport height and scroll within it.

2. **Horizontal rule conflict in inline code**: Milkdown's built-in `---` HR input rule fired even when the cursor was inside an inline code span, converting the text to an `<hr>` element unexpectedly.

3. **Clipboard formatting loss**: Copying text that contained bold, italic, strikethrough, or inline code would strip the markdown syntax and paste as plain text.

## Modifications

**Editor resize behavior** — Renamed `minHeight` to `requestedHeight` in MarkdownEditor. When content exceeds the requested height, the editor switches to a fixed height with internal scroll. Added ResizeObserver to track content height, and fixed the drag anchor to use the wrapper's visual height.

**HR suppression in inline code** — Filtered out Milkdown's built-in `insertHrInputRule` and `createCodeBlockInputRule` from the commonmark preset; replaced with custom implementations that check for inline code context.

**Clipboard markdown preservation** — Added `clipboardTextSerializer` override that runs the Milkdown serializer to preserve inline marks in `text/plain`. Extended paste detection to recognise inline markdown patterns.

**Tests** — Updated `20-markdown-editor.spec.ts` and `22-editor-resize.spec.ts` to reflect the new resize behavior and HR/clipboard fixes.

## Result

- Editor resize handle pins to a fixed viewport height with content scrolling
- `---` inside inline code no longer triggers HR conversion
- Copy/paste preserves markdown formatting (bold, italic, etc.)

author: paultuckey
body:
This PR fixes a Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the `build_album_md` function. 

Previously, user-controlled filenames were directly interpolated into Markdown image links. A malicious filename containing characters like `)` could break out of the link syntax and inject arbitrary HTML (e.g., `<script>` tags), leading to XSS if the generated Markdown was rendered in a browser.

**Changes:**
- Added `percent-encoding` crate dependency.
- Defined a `FRAGMENT` AsciiSet that includes characters dangerous to Markdown links and HTML: space, `"`, `<`, `>`, `` ` ``, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`.
- Modified `build_album_md` in `src/album.rs` to percent-encode the file path before embedding it in the Markdown string.
- Added a new test case `test_xss_injection` in `src/album.rs` that verifies that a malicious filename is correctly encoded and no longer allows injection.

**Risk:**
If left unfixed, an attacker could supply a malicious file (e.g., via a shared album or if the tool processes untrusted input) that, when processed, generates a Markdown file containing malicious scripts. If a user views this Markdown file in a viewer that executes scripts, their system or session could be compromised.

**Verification:**
- Ran `cargo test` to ensure all tests pass, including the new regression test.
- Confirmed that the malicious payload is now encoded as `%29%20%3Cscript%3E...` instead of being injected raw.

author: leonidkonev
body:
### Motivation
- The public launcher was fragile in real-world ngrok setups and could fail due to missing `DATABASE_URL`, dual-tunnel collisions (`ERR_NGROK_334`), and inspector port changes, leaving users with no public URL and confusing logs. 
- The goal is to make public sharing reliable while keeping the API bound to localhost and routing external traffic through a single, stable frontend tunnel.
- Also clean up launcher/dev helpers and make the web proxying/URL handling explicit so client code can resolve media and proxied API paths.

### Description
- `scripts/launch-public.js` now injects a safe default `DATABASE_URL`, uses one ngrok web tunnel (port 3000) only, waits for tunnel readiness via ngrok's local API, and sets public env vars (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL`, `UPLOAD_BASE_URL`, `WS_CORS_ORIGIN`) so the web app proxies backend requests through `/__api`.
- Added Next.js rewrites in `apps/web/next.config.js` to proxy `/__api/:path*` and `/socket.io/:path*` to `http://127.0.0.1:4000`, and updated `apps/web/src/lib/api.ts` with `resolveMediaUrl` to correctly resolve proxied/static media URLs.
- Improved core dev/launcher scripts and tooling: added `scripts/dev.js`, improved `scripts/launch.js` to load `.env`, added `scripts/launch-public.js`, `start-public.bat`, and enhanced `start.bat` behavior and fast-path logic.
- Backend/API hardening and feature additions: default BigInt JSON serialization, rate-limiting middleware, host binding to `HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), more robust validation in `AuthService` and DTOs, upload restrictions in `UploadsController`, new/extended endpoints for user profiles, server updates, roles permission check (`me/can-manage`), and a number of typing/defensive improvements across services and modules.
- Frontend additions and UX fixes: profile page, server settings UI, invite page, user profile page, richer `AppShell` (join/create/invite flows), message list improvements (media URL resolution), and a few package/workspace fixes in `package.json` and `apps/web/package.json`.

### Testing
- `node --check scripts/launch-public.js` ran and passed static syntax checks (success).
- `npm run build --workspace web` ran and produced a successful Next.js production build (success).
- `npm run build --workspace api` ran and completed the NestJS build (success).

### Motivation

body:
Avanza transaction history CSV exports were being imported as regular bank `Transaction` objects. They should instead create `InvestmentTransaction` records linked to `Investment` entries, since the data represents securities activity (buy/sell/dividend), not bank cashflow.

## Changes

### `AvanzaTransactionParser` — redesigned
- Removed `ICsvParser` implementation entirely
- Replaced `ParseAsync() → List<Transaction>` with `ParseTransactionsAsync() → List<AvanzaTransactionRow>`
- `AvanzaTransactionRow` DTO carries investment-specific fields: `ISIN`, `SecurityName`, `AccountNumber`, `Quantity`, `PricePerShare`, `TotalAmount` (signed), `Fees`

### `InvestmentService.ImportFromCsvAsync` — extended
- Now detects Avanza transaction history format first (before holdings parsers)
- Delegates to new private `ImportTransactionHistoryAsync()` which:
  - Creates/finds `Investment` stubs per unique security (keyed by ISIN, then name)
  - Creates `InvestmentTransaction` records per row with a security
  - Skips rows with no ISIN/security name (`Insättning`, `Uttag`, etc.)
  - Detects duplicates by `(InvestmentId, Date, TransactionType, TotalAmount)`

### `CsvImportService` — cleanup
- Removed `AvanzaTransactionParser` from the `ICsvParser` list

### `Import.razor` — UI
- Removed Avanza from the transaction bank-selection step
- Updated the Avanza investment info box to list all three supported formats (holdings per account, consolidated, **transaction history**)

### Tests & docs
- Updated `AvanzaCsvParserTests` to use `ParseTransactionsAsync()` and assert `AvanzaTransactionRow` fields (`ISIN`, `SecurityName`, `TotalAmount`, `Fees`, `Quantity`)
- `CSV_IMPORT_GUIDE.md` clarified: Avanza CSV uses the **Investeringar** import flow, not Transaktioner

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #21754

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

In #21754, the hardcoded `timezone_map` was replaced with `ZoneInfo`. On environments without the `tzdata` package, `ZoneInfo` throws an exception and silently falls back to UTC — operators have no way to tell their configured timezone is being ignored.

Rather than adding `tzdata` as a dependency, this PR adds a `verbose_logger.warning()` in the `except` block of `_setup_timezone()` to log when the fallback occurs.

- `litellm/litellm_core_utils/duration_parser.py`: Add warning log on timezone load failure
- No new dependencies, UTC fallback behavior preserved

author: cjonas9
body:
### What

Ensures the final right boundary of the fill/final filled ledger is always aligned to a checkpoint.

### Why

Previously, despite checkpoint-aligning the right frontfilling bound in runFrontfill(), this bound would be re-set to the most recent ledger in the datastore in runFrontfillChunks(). This caused noisy logs as captive core would attempt to pull a future checkpoint that hadn't yet been published, that would be resolved when that checkpoint was published. Also, this caused a rare, nondeterministic bug, where a `UNIQUE constraint violated` error could occur under the following conditions:
- backwards backfill was skipped (causing two frontfilling iterations).
- in iteration 1 of frontfilling, the unaligned datastore tip advances from the first checkpoint into the next checkpoint.
- the total amount of ledgers it advances by is < 64 ledgers.

This is unlikely in practice because, by the third bullet, it must be a small backfill (i.e. under one day of ledgers in the worst case). 

### Known limitations

N/A

## Summary
This PR fixes a responsive layout issue on the booking page around tablet/small-desktop widths (~768–1024px), where content blocks (especially pricing summary and hints) could collide or become hard to read.

## Problem
At `md` breakpoints, the booking form and result sections switched to multi-column layouts too early.  
On narrower tablet widths, this caused visual overlap and poor readability.

## Changes
### `src/pages/Booking.tsx`
- Shifted key layout breakpoints from `md` to `lg` in the booking form/result grids:
  - main form grid
  - contact/address sub-grids
  - pricing summary/hints grid
  - wide details section span
- Adjusted CTA alignment so right-alignment applies only on larger screens.
- Hardened the `Row` component used in pricing lines:
  - added spacing and alignment guards
  - prevented value column from collapsing (`shrink-0`)
  - improved behavior under constrained widths

## Why this works
Keeping the page single-column longer avoids premature horizontal compression in the 768–1024px range.  
The `Row` changes ensure label/value pairs remain readable even when space is tight.

## Validation
- `npm run lint:frontend` ✅
- `npm run build` ✅

## Scope / Risk
- Scope is limited to booking-page presentation.
- No business logic or API behavior changed.
- Low functional risk; visual/layout-only change.
