author: east-shine
body:
## Summary

Add support for `S3_KEY_PREFIX` environment variable to enable multiple expo-open-ota instances to share a single S3 bucket by partitioning objects under app-specific key prefixes.

### Changes

**`internal/bucket/bucket.go`**
- Read `S3_KEY_PREFIX` env var in `GetBucket()` and normalize trailing slash
- Pass prefix to `S3Bucket` struct via new `KeyPrefix` field

**`internal/bucket/s3Bucket.go`**
- Added `KeyPrefix` field to `S3Bucket` struct
- Added `prefixedKey()` helper method
- Applied prefix to all S3 key construction sites: listings, reads, writes, deletes, presigned URLs, and migration history

### Motivation

When running multiple expo-open-ota instances (one per app) against the same S3 bucket, there is currently no way to isolate each app's updates. This forces operators to create separate buckets per app, adding unnecessary operational overhead.

### New Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `S3_KEY_PREFIX` | Optional | Key prefix for all S3 operations (e.g., `my-app`). Trailing slash is added automatically. |

### Example Configuration

```
S3_KEY_PREFIX=my-app
```

S3 structure becomes: `my-app/{branch}/{runtimeVersion}/{timestamp}/`

### Backward Compatible

Fully backward compatible. When `S3_KEY_PREFIX` is not set or empty, all S3 paths remain unchanged.

author: copilot
body:
All API endpoints are publicly accessible with no authentication. This adds JWT-based auth infrastructure and protects all existing routes.

## New infrastructure

- **`User` model** — SQLAlchemy model with `UserRole` enum (`admin`/`reviewer`/`viewer`), `is_active`, timestamps; Alembic migration included
- **`app/auth/security.py`** — passlib/bcrypt password hashing + PyJWT token creation/verification
- **`app/auth/dependencies.py`** — `get_current_user` FastAPI dependency extracting + validating `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **`app/schemas/auth.py`** — `UserCreate` (8-char password minimum), `UserResponse`, `Token`, `LoginRequest`
- **`app/crud/user.py`** — `create_user`, `get_user_by_email`, `get_user_by_id`, `authenticate_user`

## Auth endpoints (`/api/v1/auth/`)

| Method | Path | Auth required |
|--------|------|---------------|
| POST | `/auth/register` | No |
| POST | `/auth/login` | No |
| GET | `/auth/me` | Yes |

## Protected routes

All existing endpoints in `requirements`, `test_cases`, `links`, `suggestions`, `traceability`, `analytics` now require a valid Bearer token:

```python
@router.get("/requirements")
async def list_requirements(
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),  # added
):
```

Public endpoints unchanged: `GET /`, `GET /health`.

## Startup seed

On first run (no users in DB), seeds `admin@bgstm.local` with role `admin` using `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env var (default: `admin1234`).

## Dependencies added

`PyJWT==2.10.1`, `passlib[bcrypt]==1.7.4`

> Implement backend JWT authentication for the BGSTM application as described in issue #108 ("Add Authentication and Authorization"). This PR covers the backend-only Phase 1.
> 
> ## Context
> 
> The API currently has no authentication — `reviewed_by` is a freeform string field. All endpoints are publicly accessible. This needs to be fixed before any real deployment.
> 
> ## What to Implement
> 
> ### 1. User Model (`backend/app/models/user.py`)
> Create a new `User` SQLAlchemy model following the existing patterns in the codebase:
> - Inherit from `Base` and `TimestampMixin` (see `backend/app/models/base.py`)
> - Use `GUID()` for the primary key (see `backend/app/models/suggestion.py` for the pattern)
> - Fields: `id` (UUID, PK), `email` (String, unique, indexed), `hashed_password` (String), `full_name` (String, nullable), `role` (Enum: admin/reviewer/viewer, default=viewer), `is_active` (Boolean, default=True), `created_at`, `updated_at`
> - Register the model in `backend/app/models/__init__.py`
> 
> ### 2. Auth Configuration (`backend/app/config.py`)
> Add these settings to the existing `Settings` class:
> - `SECRET_KEY: str = "change-me-in-production"` 
> - `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES: int = 30`
> - `ALGORITHM: str = "HS256"`
> 
> ### 3. Auth Utilities (`backend/app/auth/`)
> Create a new `auth` package with:
> - `security.py`: Password hashing with `passlib[bcrypt]`, JWT token creation/verification with `PyJWT`
> - `dependencies.py`: `get_current_user` FastAPI dependency that extracts and validates JWT from `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, returns the User object
> 
> ### 4. Auth Schemas (`backend/app/schemas/auth.py`)
> - `UserCreate`: email, password, full_name (optional)
> - `UserResponse`: id, email, full_name, role, is_active, created_at
> - `Token`: access_token, token_type
> - `TokenData`: user_id (optional)
> - `LoginRequest`: email, password
> 
> ### 5. Auth CRUD (`backend/app/crud/user.py`)
> - `create_user(db, user_create)` — hash password, create user
> - `get_user_by_email(db, email)` — lookup by email
> - `get_user_by_id(db, user_id)` — lookup by ID
> - `authenticate_user(db, email, password)` — verify credentials
> 
> ### 6. Auth Router (`backend/app/api/auth.py`)
> - `POST /auth/register` — create new user (public endpoint)
> - `POST /auth/login` — authenticate and return JWT token (public endpoint)
> - `GET /auth/me` — return current user info (protected endpoint)
> - Register the router in `backend/app/main.py` alongside existing routers (see line 19-25 of main.py)
> 
> ### 7. Protect All Existing Routes
> Add `current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)` to ALL existing endpoint functions in:
> - `backend/app/api/requirements.py`
> - `backend/app/api/test_cases.py`
> - `backend/app/api/links.py`
> - `backend/app/api/suggestions.py`
> - `backend/app/api/traceability.py`
> - `backend/app/api/analytics.py`
> 
> Keep these endpoints PUBLIC (no auth required):
> - `GET /` (root)
> - `GET /health`
> - `POST /auth/register`
> - `POST /auth/login`
> 
> ### 8. Alembic Migration
> - Create an Alembic migration for the new `users` table
> - If Alembic is not yet set up, initialize it with `alembic init` configured for the async SQLAlchemy engine
> 
> ### 9. Default Admin Seed
> Add a startup event or script that seeds a default admin user on first run:
> - Email: `admin@bgstm.local`
> - Password: `admin` (loaded from env var `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` with fallback)
> - Role: `admin`
> - Only create if no users exist in the database
> 
> ### 10. Dependencies
> Add to `backend/requirements.txt` (or `pyproject.toml`):
> - `PyJWT`
> - `passlib[bcrypt]`
> 
> ### 11. Tests (`backend/tests/test_auth.py`)
> - Test user registration (success + duplicate email)
> - Test login (success + wrong password + nonexistent user)
> - Test `/auth/me` with valid token
> - Test protected endpoints return 401 without token
> - Test protected endpoints work with valid token
> 
> ## Key Patterns to Follow
> 
> The existing codebase uses:
> - Async SQLAlchemy with `AsyncSession` and `Depends(get_db)` injection
> - Pydantic v2 for schemas
> - FastAPI `APIRouter` with prefix and tags
> - `GUID()` custom type for UUID primary keys
> - `TimestampMixin` for `created_at`/`updated_at`
> 
> ## Important
> - Do NOT modify `frontend/` — this is backend-only
> - Do NOT modify `eslint.config.js` or `package.json`
> - Do NOT change existing model schemas or CRUD logic (only add the auth dependency to route handlers)
> - Ensure existing tests still pass

author: auranord
body:
### Motivation
- Fix a startup parser crash (SyntaxError around the large inline SQL template literal) by removing fragile, very large SQL embedded in `src/server.js` and avoid regressions on restart. 
- Add a first-class library model and UI for managing tracks outside of playlists and ensure downloads can be queued for library-only or playlist-attached imports. 

### Description
- Moved the full DB DDL out of `src/server.js` into `src/schema.sql` and load it at startup via `const SCHEMA_SQL = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "schema.sql"), "utf8");`, then run `db.exec(SCHEMA_SQL)` in `initDb()` to avoid JS parsing issues. 
- Ensure DB parent directory exists before opening the DB via `ensureDbDirectory(DB_URL)` called prior to `new Database(DB_URL)`. 
- Introduced library support and associated API routes: `GET /api/library/tracks`, `POST /api/library/tracks`, `PUT /api/library/tracks/:id`, `DELETE /api/library/tracks/:id`, `POST /api/library/import-json`, and `GET /api/library/export`, plus import/export flows and JSON import acceptance. 
- Changed download queue semantics: added `attach_to_playlist` column and payload handling, introduced `LIBRARY_QUEUE_ID` for library-only downloads, and updated `enqueueDownload()` and download processing to respect `attach_to_playlist`. 
- Performed backward-compatible migrations and schema-alter checks in `initDb()` to add new columns (`volume_adjust_db`, `intro_sec`, `outro_sec`, `tags`, `playlist_tracks.disabled`, `download_queue.attach_to_playlist`, etc.) when missing. 
- Adjusted playlist import/export and related endpoints so imports can reference library track IDs, avoid duplicate playlist membership, and return missing IDs when library tracks are absent. 
- Frontend changes: updated `public/dashboard.html` to add library management UI (search, tag filters, import/export, add-to-playlist actions) and updated `public/player.js` to support per-track volume adjustment, intro/outro trimming and outro-based ended events. 

### Testing
- Static checks: `node --check src/server.js` and `node --check public/player.js` both passed. 
- Inline dashboard script validated by parsing with `new Function(...)` which succeeded. 
- Restart smoke test: removed `data/` then started/stopped the server twice (`rm -rf data; node src/server.js` cycles) and observed successful startup with no parser crash and proper logs; tests succeeded.

author: copilot
body:
Upgrades the trading bot and backtest engine with signal filtering, stricter risk management, smarter execution, and a side-by-side metrics report.

### Backtest engine (`backtest/engine.py`)
- **Regime detection**: ADX indicator (`_adx()`) filters out ranging markets — entries only in trending regimes (ADX > threshold)
- **Confidence scoring**: `compute_confidence()` produces a 0–1 score from RSI strength, EMA separation, trend alignment, ADX, and volume; entries below `min_confidence` are skipped
- **Risk budget**: portfolio heat check caps total open-position risk to `max_portfolio_heat` (default 6%); per-trade allocation scaled proportionally to remaining budget using `stop_loss_pct` to convert allocation to estimated risk
- **Slippage cap**: rejects entries where effective cost exceeds `max_slippage_pct`

### Bot execution (`bot.py`)
- **Decimal precision**: `_round_qty()` uses `Decimal(ROUND_DOWN)` instead of float arithmetic for exact exchange-increment compliance
- **Limit-order-first**: `USE_LIMIT_ORDERS` attempts limit orders with fill verification (`dealSize` check) before falling back to market; unfilled limit orders do not create phantom positions
- **Confidence filter**: `_is_buy_signal()` gates on `MIN_CONFIDENCE` when configured; `_compute_confidence()` uses all 5 components (RSI strength, EMA separation, trend alignment, ADX, volume) aligned with the backtest engine
- **Risk budget**: enforced in `_scan_for_entries()` with per-trade allocation capped proportionally to remaining heat via `stop_loss_pct`, consistent with backtest engine
- **Slippage cap**: enforced in `_place_market_buy()` — rejects entries and cancels orders when fill price deviates beyond `MAX_SLIPPAGE_PCT`, consistent with backtest engine behavior

### Comparison report (`backtest/__main__.py`)
- `--mode compare` runs both baseline and improved strategies on the same data, outputs a side-by-side table:

```
python -m backtest --mode compare --days 180 --seed 42
```

| Metric | Baseline | Improved | Delta |
|--------|----------|----------|-------|
| Sharpe Ratio | -4.94 | -1.54 | +3.40 |
| Max Drawdown | 98.77% | 37.27% | -61.50% |
| Trade Count | 1801 | 811 | -990 |
| Execution Costs | 105.18 | 34.83 | -70.35 |

### Config (`config.py`, `.env.example`)
- New: `MIN_CONFIDENCE`, `MAX_PORTFOLIO_HEAT`, `MAX_SLIPPAGE_PCT`, `USE_LIMIT_ORDERS`

### Tests
- 31 new tests (ADX, confidence scoring, regime filter, risk budget with per-trade capping, slippage cap rejection, Decimal rounding, compare CLI, limit order fill/unfilled/fallback) — 144 total, all passing
- CodeQL: 0 alerts

author: lico-happy
body:
## What

`dedupAndDelete` was silently deleting pinned memories when a new, very similar memory was added. Pinned memories should be immune to both `forget` and dedup.

## Why

The dedup loop checked cosine similarity but did not check the `pinned` flag. If a pinned memory scored above the 0.92 threshold against a new entry, it got queued for deletion.

## Change

One-line guard in `dedupAndDelete`: skip any candidate whose `pinned` field is true.

```go
if pinned, ok := old.Payload["pinned"].(bool); ok && pinned {
    continue
}
```

This fix was originally merged before a repo deletion rolled back main. Re-submitting to restore it.

Closes #2

author: doanbactam
body:
This PR addresses a potential Denial of Service (DoS) risk in the `POST /api/skills/report` endpoint. Previously, if the Redis service used for rate limiting was unavailable or misconfigured, the endpoint would fail with a 500 error, blocking legitimate users from submitting reports.

**Changes:**
- Modified `app/api/skills/report/route.ts` to implement a "Defense in Depth" strategy.
- Wrapped `reportRateLimit.limit()` in a `try/catch` block.
- Added a fallback to `checkRateLimitInMemory` (5 requests/hour) if Redis fails.
- Used a namespaced key (`report:${identifier}`) for the in-memory limiter to avoid collisions with other endpoints.
- Added a new test file `app/api/skills/report/route-security.test.ts` to verify that the fallback mechanism works correctly (allowing requests when Redis mocks failure, and blocking when in-memory limit is exceeded).

**Impact:**
- **Availability:** High. Ensures the reporting feature remains usable even if external dependencies (Upstash Redis) are down.
- **Security:** Maintains rate limiting protection (DoS prevention) even in degraded mode.

body:
#### O que esse PR faz?

Este PR realiza uma **refatoração estrutural nos ViewSets e Forms** do projeto, focando na padronização do ecossistema Wagtail. As principais mudanças incluem:

* **Centralização de Lógica:** Migração do `ClassicWebsiteConfigurationViewSet` para o local correto e remoção de redundâncias de filtragem de permissões nos apps `issue` e `collection`.
* **Padronização do App `team`:** Eliminação de formulários (`forms.py`) e views (`views.py`) customizados em favor do uso de classes genéricas do `core` (`CoreAdminModelForm` e `CommonControlFieldCreateView`).
* **Correção de Navegação:** Atualização de links de templates para o padrão de rotas de snippets do Wagtail.
* **Limpeza de Esquema:** Remoção do campo `bucket_app_subdir` no app de storage por obsolescência.

#### Onde a revisão poderia começar?

A revisão deve começar por **`team/models.py`** e **`team/wagtail_hooks.py`**, onde a maior parte da lógica customizada foi substituída pela herança das classes do `core`. Em seguida, verifique **`issue/wagtail_hooks.py`** para validar a simplificação da lógica de filtragem.

#### Como este poderia ser testado manualmente?

1. Acesse o painel administrativo do Wagtail.
2. Navegue até o menu de **Collections** e verifique se o link no resumo (Summary Item) do dashboard está funcionando corretamente.
3. No app **Team**, tente criar um novo `CollectionTeamMember` ou uma `Company`. Verifique se o formulário carrega corretamente e se os campos de controle (criador/editor) são preenchidos automaticamente ao salvar.
4. Verifique se a listagem de **Issues** e **TOCs** continua respeitando as permissões de usuário (filtragem por jornal).
5. Confirme se a seção de **Migration** no menu ainda exibe os itens esperados, agora com a estrutura organizada.

#### Algum cenário de contexto que queira dar?

O projeto vinha acumulando diversas implementações manuais de formulários que apenas replicavam a lógica de salvar o `request.user` nos campos `creator` e `updated_by`. Ao adotar o `CoreAdminModelForm`, reduzimos o volume de código em aproximadamente 50 linhas e centralizamos a manutenção dessas regras de auditoria no app `core`.

### Screenshots

*N/A (As mudanças são estruturais e de backend, não alterando o layout visual, exceto pela correção de links quebrados).*

## Summary
- **Unified quiet-hours logic** — Replaced duplicated inline checks in `engine.js` and `bot.js` with the shared `isQuietHours()` utility from `timeUtils.js`
- **Three-tier fallback chain** — The function now resolves through: `QUIET_HOURS_START`/`QUIET_HOURS_END` env vars (HH:mm) → YAML `config.life.quiet_hours` (integer hours) → hardcoded defaults (02:00–06:00)

The roadmap calls for "context-aware scheduling using localized configurations to keep the core codebase generalizable". This change makes quiet hours deployable per-environment (e.g. via Docker env vars or `.env`) without editing YAML — a step toward the DMN architecture.

|------|--------|
| `src/utils/timeUtils.js` | Enhanced `isQuietHours()` to accept optional config and resolve through the three-tier fallback chain |
| `src/life/engine.js` | Replaced 6-line inline check with `isQuietHours(this.config.life)` |

author: wadackel
body:
## Summary

`&mt LEFT_GUI LANG2`（親指キー）の hold-tap 設定を Karabiner-Elements の挙動に近づけるため、カスタム behavior `kht`（karabiner_hold_tap）を追加する。

### 現状の問題

Karabiner-Elements では以下の挙動を実現している:
- 素早くタップ → 英数
- 他キーと組み合わせ → 即座に Cmd+key（`lazy: true`）
- 長押し後に他キーを押さずリリース → 英数（`to_if_alone`）

一方、現在の ZMK 設定（`balanced` flavor, 160ms）では:
- 長押し後リリースしても英数にならない（`retro-tap` なし）
- 他キーの press+release を待ってから hold 判定するため、ショートカット発火が遅い

### 変更内容

`hold-preferred` + `retro-tap` + `tapping-term-ms=100` の組み合わせで Karabiner の挙動を再現:

| 設定 | 対応する Karabiner の機能 |
|------|--------------------------|
| `hold-preferred` | `lazy: true`（他キー press 時点で即座に hold 判定） |
| `retro-tap` | `to_if_alone`（他キーなしでリリースすれば英数） |
| `tapping-term-ms = 100` | `to_if_held_down_threshold_milliseconds: 100` |

適用対象: default_layer・Android・Windows の 3 箇所。既存の `&mt`（`&mt LEFT_SHIFT SPACE` 等）は変更しない。

author: robacarp
body: Since it was introduced, the rate limit concern has bothered me. It causes _a lot_ of noise because the only mechanism for it to actually prevent execution has been to throw an exception. Of course, throwing an exception _should_ abort the job, but it shouldn't be the only way to preempt a job run. I've had this in my head for many months: jobs can now be put into a Preempted state, and it'll prevent the job from executing without needing to resort to exceptional behavior for what is really ordinary circumstances. So this Introduces a distinct Preempted state to differentiate between jobs that were intentionally prevented from executing (e.g. rate limiting) and jobs that were Aborted due to unexpected errors in before hooks. - Add JobPreempted exception and Job#preempt method - Add State::Preempted to Job::State enum (not counted as executed) - Catch JobPreempted separately in Job#run, log at info instead of error - Update RateLimiter to use preempt instead of fail/retry_later - Use preempted? for rescheduling decisions in RateLimiter - Add preempted log message in observability executor - Delegate preempted? through JobRun to Job Graciously assisted by @claude Now:

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a simple, deterministic, and robust path to convert user-provided extxyz files into the batch schema required by finetuning and evaluation scripts so sweeps can actually be run. 
- Make selection of an MD seed structure trivial and reproducible, and provide a retention-benchmark packing tool for legacy holdout evaluation.
- Keep dependencies minimal and surface clear, actionable errors for missing labels or configuration issues.

### Description

- Added `scripts/make_batches_pt.py` which converts extxyz -> `.pt` batches using the same `Configuration -> AtomicData -> torch_geometric.DataLoader` flow used by training, infers keys (`REF_energy`/`energy`, `REF_forces`/`forces`, optional stress), produces `target_energy`/`target_forces`/optional `target_stress`, supports mutually-exclusive inputs (`--train_extxyz` or `--extxyz` with `--valid_fraction`), deterministic `--seed`, smoke-test caps (`--max_*_structures`), and prints dataset summaries and clear errors. 
- Added `scripts/make_retention_batches_pt.py` to produce old-domain retention `.pt` batches with deterministic subsampling (`--seed`) and optional `--max_structures` while sharing the same batch schema.
- Added `scripts/select_seed_structure.py` to choose a seed structure from extxyz with `median_natoms` (default), deterministic `random`, and `min_energy` modes, and write `.xyz` or `.extxyz` output while printing chosen index, natoms, elements and PBC presence.
- Updated `scripts/md_stability.py` to accept `.xyz` or `.extxyz` seed files by reading the first frame, and adjusted the help text accordingly.
- Added a user-facing quickstart doc `docs/QUICKSTART_DATA_PREP.md` with copy-paste commands for producing `new_domain_train_batches.pt`, optional `new_domain_valid_batches.pt`, `old_benchmark_retention_batches.pt`, and `seed_structure.xyz`/`.extxyz`, plus instructions for running sweeps, retention eval, MD stability, aggregation, and a smoke-test recipe; also added a README pointer to the quickstart.
- Added a lightweight unit test `tests/test_make_batches_pt.py` that builds tiny ASE Atoms, writes an extxyz, runs the batch-building flow and verifies the produced `.pt` loads with existing `load_batches(...)`.

### Testing

- Ran the unit test `pytest -q tests/test_make_batches_pt.py` which passed (`1 passed`) in CI-like environment. 
- Performed CLI sanity checks for help/documentation by running `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.make_batches_pt --help`, `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.make_retention_batches_pt --help`, `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.select_seed_structure --help`, and `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.md_stability --help`, which executed without error when invoked with `PYTHONPATH=.`.
- The new scripts were exercised during testing with deterministic splits and the smoke-size options to confirm they produce `.pt` files and expected summaries (no synthetic data fabricated; scripts only convert/split/pack user-provided extxyz data).

author: gnox
body:
This PR adds several major features, the most important is type 1 encryption and improvement of packet decoding.

Full list of changes:
- initial support for PowerStream
- connection can now recognize that the device uses type 1 encryption from advertisement data and successfully authenticate
- decoding of packets is now more robust - instead of blindly trusting encoded header lengths, it scans for prefixes and can handle false prefixes inside payloads by only advancing if crc16 matches
- improved error messages for config flow that occured during authentication procedure
- used AES encryption for all potentially sensitive info when sharing diagnostics, only developers have access to its private key

Thanks to @MarjovanLier that provided working initial implementation for PowerStream.

Resolves #18

Additional info from @MarjovanLier:

PowerStream uses MD5-derived keys instead of ECDH for BLE encryption. Subclasses Connection with overrides for key derivation, zero-padded AES-CBC encryption, and direct Packet framing (no EncPacket wrapper). Device stub with data_parse returning False — data streaming is a follow-up phase.

Device pushes unsolicited V19 plaintext data before responding to auth, which broke the single-shot getAuthStatus handler. Skip getAuthStatus and go straight to autoAuthentication. Handle V19 plaintext packets alongside V2/V3 encrypted packets in parseEncPackets. Set packet version to V2 to match device protocol.

PowerStream now decodes inverter_heartbeat protobuf messages from V13 BLE frames into 16 sensor fields (PV1/PV2 power/voltage/current/temp, battery level/power/temp, grid power/voltage/current/frequency, inverter temp).

Key fixes to the BLE protocol layer:
- All frame versions (V2, V3, V13) are now AES-CBC decrypted uniformly; V13 was previously treated as plaintext, causing parse failures and 5-error disconnects
- Only cmdId=0x01 heartbeats are parsed; cmdId=0x04 is a different message type that produces garbage when decoded as inverter_heartbeat

The wn511_sys_pb2.py was generated with protoc 33.2 which adds a runtime_version.ValidateProtobufRuntimeVersion check requiring protobuf >= 6.x. This breaks the import chain in HA environments with older protobuf, causing "Config flow could not be loaded".

Regenerated with protoc 24.4 to match all other _pb2.py files.

Heartbeat cmdId is 0x01 (110 fields, correct values), not 0x04 (60 fields, garbage values). Also fix auth flow to send getAuthStatus before autoAuthentication, use response=False for GATT writes to avoid 20s hang, subscribe to notifications once in initBleSessionKey, and handle max_attempts=0 correctly for BLE-level retries.

The PowerStream sends two BLE heartbeat types: cmdId=0x01 (inverter_heartbeat with full PV/battery/grid telemetry) and cmdId=0x04 (inv_heartbeat_type2 with settings/status and nested battery module data). Previously only cmdId=0x01 was handled.

Added inv_heartbeat_type2 and psdr_heartbeat_type3 proto definitions from the decompiled EcoFlow app protos, with [packed=true] for proto3 wire compatibility. Added throttled reply (10s) on cmdId=0x04 to keep the device sending data (DPU pattern). Added periodic heartbeat request loop (30s) to trigger cmdId=0x01 after auth.

- On successful per-user sync the code evaluates `_is_near_limit(...)` and schedules the next sync using `_sync_interval_seconds(...)`, and on API failures schedules a shorter retry interval to avoid long stalls and to avoid corrupting baseline/delta calculations.

body:
## 🎯 Implementação de Paginação na Busca de Produtos

### 📝 Descrição
Este PR adiciona funcionalidade de paginação na busca de produtos, permitindo que os clientes controlem a quantidade de resultados retornados e naveguem entre páginas de resultados. A resposta agora inclui metadados de paginação (total de registros, página atual e limite por página).

### 🔄 Mudanças Principais

#### 1. **Camada de Domínio**
- Atualização da interface `IProductRepository` para suportar `PaginationParams` e `OrderByDirection` no método `search`
- Alteração do retorno de `Product[]` para `PaginatedResult<Product>`

#### 2. **Camada de Infraestrutura (Repository)**
- Implementação de paginação no método `search()` do `ProductRepositoryPrisma`:
  - Cálculo de `skip` baseado em `page` e `limit`
  - Uso de `findMany` com `skip` e `take` para limitar resultados
  - Contagem total de registros com `count`
  - Ordenação por `created_at` (asc/desc)
  - Execução paralela de `findMany` e `count` usando `Promise.all` para melhor performance

#### 3. **Camada de Aplicação (Use Case)**
- `SearchProductsUseCase` atualizado para:
  - Aceitar parâmetros `page`, `limit` e `orderBy` no DTO de entrada
  - Valores padrão: `page = 1`, `limit = 10`, `orderBy = 'desc'`
  - Retornar `PaginatedResult` com metadados de paginação

#### 4. **Camada de Apresentação (Controller)**
- `SearchProductsController` atualizado para:
  - Extrair `page`, `limit` e `orderBy` dos query parameters
  - Converter strings para números com validação
  - Passar parâmetros de paginação para o use case

#### 5. **DTOs**
- `SearchProductsInputDto` expandido com:
  - `page?: number`

author: capitalrow
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce repeated 5xx/502 storms observed on the refined session page by removing duplicate background monitors, preventing DB transaction poisoning, improving error telemetry, and stopping client-side retry stampedes.
- Ensure `services.health_monitor` is started exactly once per process and cleanly stopped on shutdown to avoid thread/timer leaks and memory growth warnings.
- Make the refined `/status` path and related client loops resilient to backend failures so clients back off instead of hammering the server.

### Description

- Added a process-level singleton guard in `services/health_monitor.py` with `start_health_monitoring_once()` and `stop_health_monitoring()` plus PID-aware startup logs and a lock to prevent duplicate starts and to enable clean shutdown. The monitor is no longer started at import time in `routes/unified_transcription_api.py`.
- Moved monitored startup into `create_app()` with reloader-aware protection and wired `stop_health_monitoring()` into the app graceful shutdown hook to guarantee one monitor per process and avoid duplicate threads on reloads.
- Hardened `services/event_sequencer.py` to `rollback()` on UPSERT failures against `workspace_sequence_counter` and fallback to `workspace_seq = global_seq` when the table is missing, preventing `InFailedSqlTransaction` cascades and logging the condition.
- Improved `/api/sessions/<id>/status` in `routes/api_sessions_crown.py` with a request-id diagnostic log, `db.session.rollback()` on exceptions, and structured JSON error responses to avoid leaving DB sessions poisoned and to surface diagnostics.
- Added an after-request logger in `app.py` to record 5xx failures on refined-related endpoints for faster root-cause tracing (includes `/api/sessions/*/status` and common ETag/head endpoints used by reconciliation).
- Implemented a shared client-side “storm breaker” (`window.__minaStormBreaker`) and integrated it into `templates/session_refined.html`, `static/js/insights-notifier.js`, `static/js/reconciliation-cycle.js`, and `static/js/csrf-recovery.js` to pause polling on server 5xx, show a single UI banner, and prevent overlapping client loops from hammering the server.

### Testing

- Ran Python static sanity checks with `python -m py_compile app.py services/health_monitor.py services/event_sequencer.py routes/api_sessions_crown.py routes/unified_transcription_api.py` and the compile step completed with no syntax errors.
- Ran JavaScript syntax checks with `node --check static/js/csrf-recovery.js`, `node --check static/js/insights-notifier.js`, and `node --check static/js/reconciliation-cycle.js`, and these checks passed with no parse errors.
- Attempted a basic Playwright page navigation to capture a refined-page screenshot but the local server was not reachable in this environment (`ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE`) so an end-to-end browser check was not executed here; recommend running the manual checklist against a running staging instance to validate the full behaviour (health monitor logs, missing-table fallback, and refined storm-breaker).

body:
Full AVL binary search tree storing Arabic roots as UTF-8 keys. Each node carries the root string plus a dynamic list of validated derivative words (word + pattern + frequency counter). All four rotation cases (LL, RR, LR, RL) are implemented. 

Time Complexity is O(log n) guaranteed for insert, search and delete regardless of insertion order — critical because roots loaded from a sorted file would degenerate a plain BST to O(n).

body:
Implements the full androTrack Android app from scratch — a background GPX logger for motorcycle use — and sets the GPS polling rate to 5 Hz.

## Tracking Service
- Foreground `Service` using `LocationManager` (GPS_PROVIDER, no Play Services dependency)
- **5 Hz polling** (`minTime = 200 ms`, `minDistance = 0 f`); `LocationManager` treats this as a hint so the hardware falls back to its fastest achievable rate automatically if 5 Hz isn't supported
- Motion detection via `TYPE_LINEAR_ACCELERATION` (threshold 0.8 m/s²): recording starts on movement, stops after 20 min of inactivity
- Each session written to `track_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-mm-ss.gpx` with `<trkpt lat lon>` + `<time>`, `<speed>`, `<ele>`
- `PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK` held for the duration of a recording session

## Boot & Background
- `BootReceiver` handles `BOOT_COMPLETED` / `QUICKBOOT_POWERON` to auto-start the service
- Manifest declares `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`, `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION`, `WAKE_LOCK`

## Ride List UI
- `RideListActivity` + `RecyclerView` cards: date title, start time, duration, distance (km)

# Description

`Tab.cpp` called `line->toggle()` on a `Slic3r::GUI::Line*` — a method that does not exist on that class — breaking compilation on both MSVC and GCC.

- **Root cause:** Code added to hide the `support_style` row for the Resin-like support type used the wrong API. `Line` exposes `toggle_visible` (a data member), not a `toggle()` method.
- **Fix:** Replace the ad-hoc pattern with the existing `Tab::toggle_line()` helper, which already does the right thing:

```cpp
// Before (broken):
if (auto line = m_active_page->get_line("support_style"))
    line->toggle(!is_resin_like(support_type));   // error: no member 'toggle'

// After:
toggle_line("support_style", !is_resin_like(support_type));
```

The `build_release.yml` workflow triggers on this branch push and produces a Windows x64 NSIS installer (`.exe`) and portable (`.zip`) as CI artifacts.

N/A — compilation fix only, no UI or behaviour change.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The Class Clock and Class Mode features on the public-facing pages (home, language-arts, life-skills, etc.) are broken. Here's what's wrong:
> 
> ### 1. Class Clock Not Visible
> 
> **Root cause:** The CSS in `site/assets/css/class-clock.css` is missing `.tc-clock-dot` styles that the JavaScript (`site/assets/js/class-clock.js`) generates. The JS builds HTML with classes like `tc-clock-dot`, `tc-clock-dot--active`, `tc-clock-dot--passing`, `tc-clock-dot--before`, and `tc-clock-dot--dim`, but the CSS only has `.tc-clock-icon` — so the colored status dot never renders.
> 
> Additionally, the CSS hides `.tc-clock-period`, `.tc-clock-label`, `.tc-clock-countdown`, and `.tc-clock-sep` by default (lines 41-67), only showing them when `html.rc-class-mode-active` is set. While hiding period/label behind class mode is intentional, the **time itself and the status dot should always be visible** so users can at least see the current time.
> 
> **Fix needed in `site/assets/css/class-clock.css`:**
> - Add the missing `.tc-clock-dot` base styles (width: 8px, height: 8px, border-radius: 50%, flex-shrink: 0)
> - Add `.tc-clock-dot--active` (green), `.tc-clock-dot--passing` (yellow), `.tc-clock-dot--before` (blue), `.tc-clock-dot--dim` (gray) color variants
> - Ensure `.tc-clock-time` and `.tc-clock-dot` are always visible (not gated by class mode)
> - Keep period, label, countdown, and separator hidden behind `html.rc-class-mode-active` as intended
> 
> ### 2. Class Clock Init Timing Race Condition
> 
> **Root cause:** `site/assets/js/class-clock.js` tries to find `.tc-topbar` on DOMContentLoaded, but `public-nav.js` (which injects the topbar) may not have finished yet. The `class-mode.js` already uses a double-defer pattern (`requestAnimationFrame` + `setTimeout`) to handle this — `class-clock.js` needs the same pattern.
> 
> **Fix needed in `site/assets/js/class-clock.js`:**
> - Change the init from direct `DOMContentLoaded` → `init()` to use the double-defer pattern:
> ```js
> function deferInit() {
>   requestAnimationFrame(function () { setTimeout(init, 0); });
> }
> if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
>   document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', deferInit);
> } else {
>   deferInit();
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 3. Class Mode PIN Is Wrong
> 
> **Root cause:** `site/web/class-mode.js` line 15 has `var CLASS_MODE_PIN = '1234';` — this needs to be changed to `'6278'`.
> 
> **Fix needed in `site/web/class-mode.js`:**
> - Change `var CLASS_MODE_PIN = '1234';` to `var CLASS_MODE_PIN = '6278';`
> 
> ### 4. Class Mode Should Be a Bottom Tab on the Main Page
> 
> **Current behavior:** Class Mode appears as a button at the bottom of the sidebar navigation.
> 
> **Desired behavior:** Class Mode should be a **tab at the bottom of the main page** that opens so the user can enter the PIN (6-2-7-8). It should work like a pull-up tab/drawer anchored to the bottom of the page content area, not hidden inside the sidebar.
> 
> **Fix needed in `site/web/class-mode.js` and `site/assets/css/class-mode.css`:**
> - Move the Class Mode widget from appending to `.tc-sidebar` to appending to `.tc-main` (or the main content area / body)
> - Restyle it as a fixed bottom tab/drawer that:
>   - Shows a small "Class Mode" tab handle at the bottom of the page
>   - When clicked, slides up to reveal the PIN entry form
>   - When the correct PIN (6278) is entered, activates class mode (adds `rc-class-mode-active` to html)
>   - The tab should be visible on all public pages (not teacher/admin/substitute)
>   - Should look clean and match the existing dark theme (use rc-theme.css variables)
> 
> ## Files to modify:
> 1. `site/assets/css/class-clock.css` — Add missing dot styles, fix visibility rules
> 2. `site/assets/js/class-clock.js` — Fix init timing with double-defer pattern
> 3. `site/web/class-mode.js` — Change PIN to '6278', move widget to bottom tab on main page instead of sidebar
> 4. `site/assets/css/class-mode.css` — Restyle as bottom page tab/drawer instead of sidebar widget
> 
> ## Important context:
> - The Supabase `class_schedule` table now exists (just created), so the Supabase fetch should work going forward
> - The fallback to `site-state.json` also works and has 8 periods defined
> - `public-nav.js` dynamically injects the topbar and sidebar on public pages
> - `class-clock.js` dynamically imports `class-schedule.js` (ES module) via `import('/web/class-schedule.js')`
> - The site uses CSS custom properties from `rc-theme.css`: `--rc-brand: #35e08a`, `--rc-ink: #e8f1ec`, `--rc-ink-dim: #a9bbb1`, `--rc-border`, `--rc-glass`, etc.
> - The `class_schedule` Supabase table schema: `id`, `hour_number`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `label`, `is_planning`, `active`, `sort_order`
> - Pages that include these scripts: `site/index.html`, `site/language-arts/index.html`, `site/life-skills/index.html`, `site/student/index.html`, `site/substitute/index.html`, `site/math-toolkit/index.html`

author: adelkheniche
body:
### Motivation
- Cross-device WebRTC sessions were failing in production due to a single public signaling endpoint and lack of a resilient fallback, causing empty sessions across browsers and devices. 
- The goal is to improve real-world reliability while keeping a strict "zero account / zero self-host" constraint.

### Description
- Add multiple public WebRTC signaling endpoints by default and allow custom comma-separated `signaling` URLs via query string or `planner_signaling_url` in localStorage. (files: `docs/index.html`, `docs/realtime.js`).
- Implement an automatic fallback path from WebRTC to a public WebSocket relay when no remote peer appears after a configurable timeout, using a public fallback endpoint defaulting to `wss://demos.yjs.dev`. The fallback is configurable via `fallback`, `fallbackDelayMs`, and `publicWs` query params or corresponding localStorage keys. (files: `docs/index.html`, `docs/realtime.js`).
- Provide a robust provider switch that rebinds `awareness` and preserves presence/drag behavior after switching from `WebrtcProvider` to `WebsocketProvider`. (files: `docs/index.html`, `docs/realtime.js`).
- Unify runtime parameter parsing and expose new URL/localStorage knobs: `fallback`, `fallbackDelayMs`, `publicWs` / `planner_public_ws_endpoint`, `planner_rt_fallback`, `planner_rt_fallback_delay`. (files: `docs/index.html`, `docs/realtime.js`, `README.md`).
- Minor WebRTC tuning: increase `maxConns` for `WebrtcProvider` and expose a public websocket resolver for zero-config fallback. (files: `docs/index.html`).

### Testing
- Static JS sanity check of `docs/realtime.js` with `node --check` succeeded. (status: passed)
- Repository diff check (`git diff --check`) passed with no whitespace/syntax issues. (status: passed)
- Extracted browser script contains JSX and failed `node --check` as expected because it requires Babel transpilation, so this failure is expected and not indicative of the runtime changes. (status: expected failure)
- No runtime browser automated tests were run; changes are limited to client-side runtime configuration and were validated by static checks above.

author: forkwright
body:
## What

Buffers `text_delta` and `thinking_delta` SSE events, flushing to reactive state at most every 100ms instead of on every event. This bounds markdown re-parsing from per-character to ~10Hz.

## Why

Each `text_delta` event triggers a Svelte reactivity update → `<Markdown>` re-renders → `marked.parse()` + `DOMPurify.sanitize()` on the full accumulated string. At streaming speed this is 20-50+ parses/sec of a growing string. The 100ms debounce reduces this to ~10 parses/sec with no perceptible latency.

## How

- Added `_textBuffer`, `_thinkingBuffer`, `_flushTimer` to `AgentChatState`
- `text_delta` / `thinking_delta` append to buffer and schedule a debounced flush
- `turn_complete` / `turn_abort` flush immediately before consuming text
- All reset paths clear buffers and cancel timers

## Testing

- Build passes, no new type errors
- Streaming text should appear smooth at ~10fps instead of per-character
- Immediate flush on turn_complete ensures no text is lost
- Abort mid-stream preserves buffered text in partial message

Spec 29 Phase 2.

body:
Creating a company fails with `Could not find the 'address_line1' column of 'companies' in the schema cache` because the live Supabase database is missing address and metadata columns that the app expects, causing PostgREST to reject inserts.

## Changes

- **`supabase/migrations/009_fix_companies_address_columns.sql`** — idempotent migration that:
  - Conditionally adds missing columns to `public.companies`: `address_line1`, `address_line2`, `city`, `postcode`, `country` (default `'UK'`), `status` (default `'active'`), `company_type` (default `'standard'`)
  - Emits `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'` to flush the PostgREST schema cache immediately on apply

```sql
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_schema = 'public'
      AND table_name   = 'companies'
      AND column_name  = 'address_line1'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.companies ADD COLUMN address_line1 text;
  END IF;
  -- ... repeated for address_line2, city, postcode, country, status, company_type
END
$$;

NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
```

Apply by running the migration in the Supabase SQL Editor.

body:
`HSMKeyProviderAdapter::wrapDEK` was calling `sign()` (wrong primitive) and `unwrapDEK` returned a freshly-generated random key on every call — making field-level encryption non-functional since wrap and unwrap never produced a matching key pair.

## Core Fix

**`src/security/hsm_key_provider_adapter.cpp`**
- `wrapDEK`: `hsm_->sign()` → `hsm_->encryptData()` (RSA public-key encrypt / AES-GCM in stub mode)
- `unwrapDEK`: `RAND_bytes()` stub → `hsm_->decryptData()` (deterministic round-trip)

## New API: `HSMProvider::encryptData` / `decryptData`

author: ricardoparro
body:
## Summary
Fixes #537 - Mobile Total Blocking Time Above Target (250ms)

## Problem
Mobile TBT was 250ms, exceeding the 200ms target due to:
- 7 long main-thread tasks found by PageSpeed
- 9 non-composited animations
- ~160KB of unused JavaScript on initial load
- Heavy synchronous JS execution blocking interactivity

## Solution

### 1. Code Splitting for Data Modules (~77KB deferred)
Converted 4 heavy data modules from synchronous imports to dynamic imports:

| Module | Size | Status |
|--------|------|--------|
| bands.js | 24KB | ✅ Lazy loaded |
| genres.js | 24KB | ✅ Lazy loaded |
| birthdays.js | 16KB | ✅ Lazy loaded |
| gearComparisons.js | 13KB | ✅ Lazy loaded |

### 2. Compositor-Friendly CSS Animations
- Changed shimmer animation from `background-position` to `transform`
- Added `will-change: transform` for GPU acceleration
- Moves animation work to compositor thread, reducing main thread blocking

### 3. Content Visibility Optimizations
- Added `content-visibility: auto` for below-fold content
- Added `contain: layout style paint` for complex sections
- Defers rendering of off-screen content

### 4. Idle-Time Preloading
- Data modules preloaded via `requestIdleCallback` after page interactive
- Graceful loading states prevent UI flash during lazy loading
- 3-second timeout fallback for browsers without `requestIdleCallback`

## Bundle Impact
| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|
| Main bundle | 937KB | 859KB | -78KB |
| Code-split chunks | 6 | 10 | +4 new |
| Deferred JS | 0KB | 77KB | +77KB on-demand |

## New Chunk Files
```
bands-*.js (24.1 kB)
birthdays-*.js (16.4 kB)
gearComparisons-*.js (12.8 kB)
genres-*.js (23.5 kB)
```

- [x] Build succeeds with expo export
- [x] Code-split chunks created correctly
- [x] Loading states display for lazy pages
- [x] Preloading triggers during idle time

- #535 - Mobile LCP Performance

author: copilot
body:
Two bugs combined to show incorrect totals for Lucileide (R$1,274 instead of ~R$987) and wrong "Ainda a pagar" (R$574 instead of ~R$287).

### Bug 1 — `remainingBrl` cross-rate inconsistency (`payments.html`)

`totalBrl` used the live rate while `paidBrl` used the fallback rate, making their difference numerically wrong. The fix computes remaining directly from the net unpaid shares:

```js
// Before
const remainingBrl = totalBrl - paidBrl;  // mixes live vs. fallback rate

// After
const remainingBrl = (tot.brl - paid.brl) + (tot.chf - paid.chf) * rate;
```

### Bug 2 — Stale JSON data served from browser/CDN cache (`assets/public.js`)

The module-level `_cache` object and browser HTTP cache were both preventing updated `expenses.json` from loading after data fixes. Removed `_cache` entirely and added `{ cache: 'no-store' }` to all `fetch()` calls in both `loadJson` and `fetchContent`.

### Test coverage (`tests/split.test.js`)

Added test 19: integration test against the real E5/E6/E11 expense data asserting Lucileide (`tot.brl ≈ 986.81`, `paid.brl ≈ 699.77`, `remaining ≈ 287.04`) and Jhemerson (`remaining ≈ 0`).

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem to fix definitively
> 
> The payments page (https://stadelmann77.github.io/Voyage-BR-2026/payments.html) still shows wrong totals for Lucileide (R$1,274 instead of ~R$987) and wrong "Ainda a pagar" (R$574 instead of ~R$287).
> 
> ## Root causes identified (2 bugs)
> 
> ### Bug 1 — Wrong `remainingBrl` formula in `payments.html` line 286
> 
> Current code:
> ```js
> const totalBrl     = tot.brl  + tot.chf  * rate;          // line 284
> const paidBrl      = paid.brl + paid.chf * fallbackRate;  // line 285
> const remainingBrl = totalBrl - paidBrl;                  // line 286 — BUG
> ```
> 
> The problem: `totalBrl` uses live `rate` but `paidBrl` uses `fallbackRate`. Their difference is numerically inconsistent. More importantly: `remainingBrl` must be computed independently from the net unpaid shares, not derived from the cross-rate subtraction.
> 
> **Fix for line 286:**
> ```js
> const remainingBrl = (tot.brl - paid.brl) + (tot.chf - paid.chf) * rate;
> ```
> 
> ### Bug 2 — Stale browser/CDN cache of `data/expenses.json`
> 
> `assets/public.js` caches JSON responses in a module-level `_cache` object AND relies on browser HTTP cache. After PR 16 fixed `data/expenses.json`, the page at stadelmann77.github.io still serves the old cached file.
> 
> **Fix in `assets/public.js`:** In the `loadJson` function, change the fetch to bypass cache:
> ```js
> // BEFORE:
> const res = await fetch(`data/${key}.json`);
> 
> // AFTER:
> const res = await fetch(`data/${key}.json`, { cache: 'no-store' });
> ```
> 
> Also remove or bypass the module-level `_cache` for all data files (or at minimum for `expenses`), so every page load fetches fresh data from GitHub Pages.
> 
> The `_cache` map (`const _cache = {};`) should be removed from `loadJson`. The `fetchContent` function has its own separate cache logic and should also use `{ cache: 'no-store' }`.
> 
> ## Expected result after fix
> 
> For Lucileide (beneficiary of E5, E6, E11 — after PR 16 set amount_chf=null on all lodging expenses):
> - `tot.brl = 1300.17/3 + 799.14/3 + 861.12/3 = 433.39 + 266.38 + 287.04 = 986.81`
> - `tot.chf = 0` (all null)
> - `paid.brl = 433.39 + 266.38 = 699.77` (E5+E6 are ✅)
> - `paid.chf = 0`
> - `totalBrl = 986.81`
> - `paidBrl = 699.77`
> - `remainingBrl = (986.81 - 699.77) + 0 = 287.04` ✅
> 
> ## Files to change
> 
> ### `payments.html` — line 286 only
> Change:
> ```js
> const remainingBrl = totalBrl - paidBrl;
> ```
> To:
> ```js
> const remainingBrl = (tot.brl - paid.brl) + (tot.chf - paid.chf) * rate;
> ```
> 
> ### `assets/public.js` — `loadJson` function
> 1. Remove the module-level `_cache` object and all `_cache[key]` read/write references inside `loadJson`
> 2. Change `fetch(`data/${key}.json`)` to `fetch(`data/${key}.json`, { cache: 'no-store' })`
> 3. In `fetchContent`, also change `fetch(`data/${key}.json`)` to use `{ cache: 'no-store' }` and remove its local cache logic
> 
> ### `tests/split.test.js`
> Add a new integration-style test (test 20 or similar) that:
> 1. Simulates the full expense list from `data/expenses.json` (after PR 16) with amount_chf=null for E7-E11
> 2. Computes `personTotals` and `paidTotals` for all people using `computeSplit` and `getEffectivePaidRatio`
> 3. Asserts Lucileide: tot.brl ≈ 986.81, paid.brl ≈ 699.77, remaining ≈ 287.04
> 4. Asserts Jhemerson: tot.brl ≈ (1300.17+799.14)/3 = 699.77, paid.brl ≈ 699.77, remaining ≈ 0
>

## Summary

Adds auth configuration and the `internal/auth` package for session management and Google token verification.

### Changes

**Config (`internal/config/config.go`)**
- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` (required)
- `SESSION_SECRET` (required, minimum 32 bytes enforced at init)
- `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (default `shiru_session`)
- `SESSION_TTL` (default `72h`)

**Session Manager (`internal/auth/session.go`)**
- HMAC-SHA256 signed cookie: `base64url(payload).base64url(signature)`
- Payload: `{"user_id": "uuid", "exp": unix_timestamp}`
- Constant-time signature comparison via `hmac.Equal`
- Rejects nil UUIDs, expired sessions (`exp <= now`), and short secrets

**Google Verifier (`internal/auth/google.go`)**
- Wraps `google.golang.org/api/idtoken` to validate ID tokens against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
- Extracts sub, email, name, picture claims

- 8 test cases: round-trip, expired, tampered payload, tampered signature, wrong secret, invalid formats, short secret rejection, nil UUID rejection

author: copilot
body:
Implements Phase 2 roadmap item: delta (binary diff) updates for the `updates` module. Instead of downloading full replacement files, the engine applies binary patches to installed files — expected 70–90% bandwidth reduction for incremental releases.

## Description

### `DeltaUpdateEngine` (`include/updates/delta_update_engine.h`, `src/updates/delta_update_engine.cpp`)
Two patch algorithms, both pure C++ with no new dependencies (zstd already bundled):
- **ZSTD_DICT** — base file as `ZSTD_CDict`/`ZSTD_DDict`; best ratio for similar binaries
- **VCDIFF** — hash-table-accelerated COPY/ADD delta, zstd-compressed instruction stream
- BSDIFF/XDELTA3 entries fall back to ZSTD_DICT (external libs not bundled)

`applyDelta` pipeline per file: validate path → verify base SHA-256 → locate pre-staged patch → apply → verify target SHA-256 + size → `fs::rename` (atomic). Failed files go to `files_fallback`; remaining files continue.

```cpp
DeltaUpdateEngine engine(install_dir, download_dir);
engine.registerDelta(delta_manifest_from_release_asset);
auto result = engine.applyDelta(*engine.findDelta("1.4.0", "1.5.0"));
// result.files_fallback → needs conventional full download
```

### Security fix — path traversal in `applyDelta`
`fd.path` from untrusted JSON manifest was used raw in `fs::path` construction. `isSafePath()` now rejects: empty, absolute, any `..` component, and paths whose `weakly_canonical` form escapes the sandbox (including the `/install` vs `/installmalicious/` prefix-trick).

### Build
- `delta_update_engine.cpp` added to `cmake/CMakeLists.txt` and `cmake/ModularBuild.cmake`

tracking issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44930
cc target maintainer @Patryk27

I ran into multiple issues, and although with this PR and a little harness I can run the test with qemu on avr, the implementation is perhaps not ideal.

The problem we found is that on `avr` the `c_int/c_uint` types are `i16/u16`, and this was not handled in the c-variadic checks. Luckily there is a field in the target configuration that contains the targets `c_int_width`. However, this field is not actually used in `core` at all, there the 16-bit targets are just hardcoded.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1500f0f47f5fe8ddcd6528f6c6c031b210b4eac5/library/core/src/ffi/primitives.rs#L174-L185

Perhaps we should expose this like endianness and pointer width?

author: copilot
body:
Adds the full GLSL post-process pipeline for the VsTube CRT renderer and a modular TypeScript configuration layer to drive it.

## GLSL passes (`shaders/`)

| Pass | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Glyph composite | `glyph-composite.glsl` | Atlas sample → fg/bg blend → premultiplied RGBA |
| Bright-pass | `bright-pass.glsl` | Quadratic soft-knee luminance threshold for bloom input |
| Separable blur | `bloom.glsl` | 13-tap Gaussian; single shader, `uDirection` selects H/V |
| Chromatic aberration | `chromatic-aberration.glsl` | Radial per-channel UV offset |
| Scanline | `scanline.glsl` | sin²-based raster modulation |
| Noise | `noise.glsl` | Per-frame animated grain via GPU hash — no noise texture |
| Vignette | `vignette.glsl` | smoothstep edge darkening; outer edge computed dynamically to guarantee `edge0 < edge1` |
| Curvature | `curvature.glsl` | Barrel warp with `uBorderColor` corner mask |
| Composite | `composite.glsl` | Additive bloom blend + multiplicative phosphor tint |

## Pipeline module (`packages/framework/src/pipeline/`)

- **`pipelineConfig.ts`** — typed per-pass config interfaces, `defaultPipelineConfig()`, and `parsePipelineConfig()` with range-clamping and NaN fallback
- **`shaderPipeline.ts`** — `ShaderPipeline` wraps an ordered pass list; exposes `activePasses` for the render loop and `reconfigure()` for hot-reload without object re-creation

```ts
const pipeline = new ShaderPipeline(parsePipelineConfig(rawSettings));

for (const pass of pipeline.activePasses) {
  renderer.bindUniforms(pass.uniforms);
  renderer.drawFullScreenQuad(pass.shaderFile);
}

// Later, on settings change:
pipeline.reconfigure(parsePipelineConfig(updatedSettings));
```

## VS Code settings

15 new `vstube.pipeline.*` contribution points — one `enabled` toggle plus numeric parameters per pass — wired to the types in `pipelineConfig.ts`.

### Motivation
- Add an interactive candlestick chart to the Trade Detail view using TradingView Lightweight Charts so clicking a trade shows price action and entry/exit markers. 
- Keep the change narrowly scoped to the Trade Detail/chart behavior and make the UI degrade gracefully if the chart module is not present.

### Description
- Implemented a `TradeChart` that dynamically imports `lightweight-charts`, calls `createChart(container, options)`, adds a candlestick series via the docs-style `chart.addSeries(CandlestickSeries, options)` with a compatibility fallback to `chart.addCandlestickSeries`, and calls `chart.timeScale().fitContent()` afterwards (changes in `edge-journal/src/App.jsx`).
- Map the app's mock/fetch candle objects into the required series shape using UNIX-second `time` values, and attach entry/exit markers via `series.setMarkers(...)` when timestamps are present.
- Make the chart responsive with a `ResizeObserver` that updates `chart.applyOptions({ width: ... })`, and ensure proper cleanup on unmount via `chart.remove()`; if the module import fails the chart container shows a friendly advisory message.
- Wire the existing `fetchCandles`/trade-click flow so selecting a trade triggers candle fetch and the `TradeChart` receives `candles`, `entrySec`, and `exitSec`; also expose and use an `onClearTradeNotes` callback to clear review inputs for the selected trade when requested (all changes are in `edge-journal/src/App.jsx`).

author: mattarderne
body:
Introduces a configurable approval layer that adds friction to irreversible
("one-way door") operations in the lending workflow, inspired by Anthropic's
agent autonomy research on proportional oversight for high-stakes actions.

One-way doors identified and gated:
- deal.stage_advance / deal.stage_override (stage transitions)
- loan.approve / loan.disburse / loan.write_off / loan.close
- facility.approve / facility.delete
- covenant.waive

Gate modes (configurable per org and per loan line):
- auto: no friction, action proceeds immediately
- human: requires one human approval (maker-checker)
- dual: requires two separate approvers

Key features:
- Per-tenant (org) and per-loan-line configuration
- Amount-based thresholds (e.g., gate only above $1M)
- Stage-scoped policies (e.g., only gate during closing)
- Priority-based policy resolution (specific overrides general)
- Self-approval prevention (cannot approve your own request)
- Emergency bypass with mandatory rationale and audit trail
- Full audit trail for all gate events (GATE_REQUIRED, GATE_APPROVED,
  GATE_REJECTED, GATE_BYPASSED, GATE_PARTIAL_APPROVAL)
- X-Gate-Record-Id header pattern for retry-after-approval flow

New files:
- packages/core/src/services/approval-gate.ts (ApprovalGateService)
- packages/api/src/routes/gates.ts (API endpoints)
- packages/cli/src/commands/gates.ts (CLI commands)

author: newhook
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where pi agent sessions would sometimes exit without calling `sarge complete`, leaving tasks permanently stuck in `processing` status.

## Problem

When sarge dispatches work to the pi agent, the agent is expected to call `sarge complete <task-id>` before exiting. However, in some cases the agent would exit (cleanly or otherwise) without making this call, leaving the task stranded. This required manual intervention to unstick the workflow.

## Solution

Implements a **defense-in-depth** approach with two complementary safety nets:

### 1. Pi Extension — Primary Safety Net (`.pi/extensions/sarge-complete.ts`)
A new pi extension that hooks into the agent lifecycle:
- **`agent_end`** — Fires after the LLM finishes processing. Checks if the task (identified via `SARGE_TASK_ID` env var) is still in `processing` status, and if so, calls `sarge complete --error` to mark it as failed with a descriptive message.
- **`session_shutdown`** — Secondary hook as a backup for interactive sessions.
- Fully idempotent: if `sarge complete` was already called by the agent, the task won't be in `processing` status, so this is a no-op.

### 2. Environment Variable Passing (`internal/agents/pi/pi.go`)
Sets `SARGE_TASK_ID` environment variable on the pi agent subprocess so the extension knows which task it's responsible for without parsing the prompt.

### 3. Server-Side Fallback (`internal/agents/runner/runner.go`)
In `handleAgentExit()`, when the agent process exits but the task is still in `processing` status, the runner marks it as failed. This catches cases where pi crashes entirely and the extension never fires.

## Beads Resolved

- **ac-l7g** — pi sometimes get stuck (root issue)
- **ac-l7g.1** — Create pi extension to call sarge complete on session_shutdown
- **ac-l7g.2** — Pass task ID as environment variable to pi agent
- **ac-l7g.3** — Add server-side fallback for all task types when agent exits without completing

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.pi/extensions/sarge-complete.ts` | New pi extension with `agent_end` and `session_shutdown` hooks |
| `internal/agents/pi/pi.go` | Pass `SARGE_TASK_ID` env var to agent subprocess |
| `internal/agents/runner/runner.go` | Server-side fallback to fail stuck tasks on agent exit |

## Testing Notes

- The extension is idempotent — safe to deploy immediately
- The server-side fallback only triggers when task status is still `processing`, avoiding double-completion
- Both safety nets log descriptive error messages for debugging
- Recommended: test with a pi session that exits without calling `sarge complete` to verify the fallback chain fires correctly

body:
Three bugs causing incorrect BRL totals for Lucileide and Jhemerson on the payments page: a rate-mixing formula, a stale in-memory/HTTP cache masking updated expense data, and a missing regression test.

## Changes

- **`payments.html` — `remainingBrl` formula fix**
  Old formula subtracted totals computed at two different rates (live vs. fallback), producing an incorrect remainder whenever `paid.chf > 0`:
  ```js
  // Before — mixes live rate (totalBrl) and fallback rate (paidBrl)
  const remainingBrl = totalBrl - paidBrl;

  // After — net CHF difference converted at a single rate
  const remainingBrl = (tot.brl - paid.brl) + (tot.chf - paid.chf) * rate;
  ```

- **`assets/public.js` — remove stale caching**
  - Deleted module-level `_cache` object and all read/write lines in `loadJson` and `fetchContent`
  - Added `{ cache: 'no-store' }` to every `fetch` call so updated `expenses.json` is always fetched fresh from the server

- **`tests/split.test.js` — Test 19: Lucileide actual-data regression**
  Uses real expense data (E5, E6, E11 with `amount_chf: null`) to assert:
  - `tot.brl ≈ 986.81` (433.39 + 266.38 + 287.04)
  - `paid.brl ≈ 699.77` (E5 + E6 only, E11 unpaid)
  - `remainingBrl ≈ 287.04` via the corrected formula

author: ademczuk
body:
![TUI inline image rendering on v2026.3.3 — left: Docker TUI terminal with iTerm2 graphics, right: WebUI Control UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ademczuk/openclaw/feat/tui-inline-image-rendering/docs/images/tui-inline-image-v2026.3.3-rebase-proof.png)

> **Rebased onto main (v2026.3.3)** — squash-rebased from 22 commits to 1 clean commit. All 103 tests pass on openclaw 2026.3.3. Screenshot above confirms inline image rendering working after rebase — Docker TUI terminal (left) and WebUI Control UI (right) both rendering agent-generated images inline.

## Quick Summary
This adds inline image rendering to the TUI via iTerm2/Kitty graphics protocol. When the image tool runs inside Docker, the agent's images appear directly in the terminal instead of just showing file paths.

The PR is structured in clear sections:

- Image tool emission (2 files) -- adds base64 image blocks alongside MEDIA: text
- Sanitize bypass (1 file) -- preserves image data when MEDIA blocks are present
- Gateway MEDIA filter (1 file) -- passes image data through verbose filtering
- TUI rendering (2 files) -- renders images inline using pi-tui
- WebUI tool events + dedup (2 files) -- live image delivery and duplicate prevention

Squash-rebased onto current upstream/main (v2026.3.3). All 103 feature tests pass. 0 merge conflicts.
## What

OpenClaw Pi currently shows text placeholders like `[image/jpeg 42kb]` when agents use the image tool because the event pipeline strips image data before it reaches Pi's renderer. This PR unblocks that pipeline so Pi renders images inline using pi-tui's Image component, meaning users in WezTerm, iTerm2, Ghostty or Kitty see exactly what the agent is looking at right inside their terminal session. The bypasses only activate on image tool results and the entire render path is behind pi-tui's terminal capability check, so nothing changes for terminals without graphics support.

The web Control UI also benefits: after an agent run that produces images, the chat history reloads with injected base64 images so users see rendered images in the browser too.

## The three choke points and fixes

| Choke point | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `sanitizeToolResult` | Strips base64 `data` from image blocks | Counts MEDIA paths + bare image blocks, preserves via quota |
| Gateway verbose filter | Deletes `data.result` at default verbosity | Preserves result when MEDIA text lines or inline image blocks present |
| TUI renderer | Only had file-path rendering | Added two-stage: file path first, base64 fallback with adjacency-based dedup |

## Post-merge fixes (after rebasing onto main)

After merging `upstream/main` (commit `bef1e64e1d`), two critical fixes that were working before the merge needed to be re-applied because upstream changes to `chat.ts` and the gateway's history/sanitization pipeline created new code paths that didn't include the image-specific guards:

### Deduplication regression

The merge brought in upstream refactors to `chat.ts` that reset the injection pipeline's state tracking. Three dedup layers had to be re-applied against the new code structure:

| Fix | Why it regressed |
|-----|------------------|
| **`seenPaths` preservation** across `tool_use` boundaries | Upstream restructured the message-walk loop -- the old `seenPaths.clear()` call on `hasToolUse` assistant messages was in a different branch position after merge, wiping the dedup set between the agent's internal `find` + `view-image` sub-steps |
| **`seen64` fingerprint dedup** (first 64 chars of base64) | This was a new layer added pre-merge that had to be re-integrated into both injection sites within `injectMediaImagesIntoHistory` after the upstream refactor changed the function's internal structure |
| **`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock` recursion** into nested `content[]` | Upstream's sanitizer changes didn't recurse into `tool_result.content[]` arrays -- browser-side `extractImages` DOES recurse, so unsanitized nested image blocks caused duplicates on chat history reload |

### Auto-refresh regression

The WebUI `caps: ["tool-events"]` declaration in `gateway.ts` was lost during the merge because upstream touched the same connect handshake block. Without this capability declaration, the gateway never registered the WebUI connection for tool stream events, so:

1. Tool events with image data never reached the browser
2. `chatRunHasMedia` flag was never set client-side
3. The conditional history reload (`shouldReloadHistoryForFinalEvent`) never fired
4. Images only appeared after a manual page refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R)

The fix was straightforward -- re-add `caps: ["tool-events"]` to the connect handshake -- but the root cause was non-obvious because the merge resolved cleanly (no conflict markers), yet silently dropped the capability array contents back to `[]`.

## Impact scope

This PR only affects the **TUI terminal renderer** and **WebUI Control UI** image paths. It does **not** affect:

- **Telegram** -- uses its own message adapter (`telegram-adapter.ts`) which formats tool results as text; image blocks are handled by Telegram's native photo API, not MEDIA: protocol
- **WhatsApp** -- uses its own bridge adapter; image delivery goes through WhatsApp's media upload API
- **Slack** -- uses Slack block kit for message formatting; images are uploaded as files/unfurls
- **Discord** -- uses Discord embeds/attachments for images via its own adapter

The MEDIA: protocol and `sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock` changes are scoped to the gateway's `chat.history` method (WebUI reload path) and the TUI's `handleToolExecutionEnd` renderer. External messaging adapters have their own image handling that does not intersect with this pipeline.

## Why it's safe

- Everything behind `canRenderInlineImages()` which checks `pi-tui getCapabilities().images`. If null, entire codepath is dead.
- `sanitizeToolResult` bypass uses a quota: `Math.max(mediaPathCount, imageBlockCount)` to cover both local (MEDIA + image block) and web-only (bare image block) sources. Extra blocks are stripped normally.
- Gateway verbose filter checks for both MEDIA text lines and `{ type: "image" }` blocks with data. No redundant bypass paths.
- `validateMediaPath` rejects null bytes, non-image extensions, non-regular files, empty files, >6MB (`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`) before any `readFileSync`.
- `readImageAsBase64` has TOCTOU defense: re-checks buffer size after `readFile` to catch races between `lstat` and `readFile`.
- `file://` URIs normalized via `normalizeMediaSource` before path validation.
- `sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock` recurses into nested content arrays for defense in depth.
- No new dependencies.

## Hardening (5 review sessions)

### Security and correctness

| Fix | Severity | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| TOCTOU race in `readImageAsBase64` | Medium | Re-check buffer size after `readFile` to catch file replacement between `lstat` and read |
| `seenPaths` dedup across tool_use boundaries | High | Paths lost when `seenPaths.clear()` fired on `hasToolUse` assistant messages -- agent multi-step commands (find + view-image) produced duplicates. Now preserves seenPaths across tool_use rounds |
| `seen64` base64 fingerprint dedup | Medium | Second dedup layer using first-64-char fingerprints -- catches identical images from different strategies (file read vs base64 passthrough) |
| `sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock` recursion | High | Only stripped top-level image blocks -- nested `tool_result.content[]` image blocks survived sanitization and caused duplicates on browser-side `extractImages` recursion |
| WebUI `caps: ["tool-events"]` missing | High | Client never declared tool-events capability -- gateway never sent tool stream events -- images only appeared after manual page refresh |
| `pendingImages` lost at end of history | Medium | Reverse-scan flush into last assistant message when history ends without qualifying text-only assistant |
| TUI image dedup | Medium | Single-pass adjacency-b

- **Задача**: Сглаживание изображения
- **Вариант**: 22
- **Технология**:  SEQ, MPI
- **Описание** Реализована последовательная и параллельная версии алгоритма сглаживания изображения с использованием ядра Гаусса 3×3. Последовательный алгоритм выполняет свертку изображения с ядром, обходя все пиксели тройным циклом и применяя весовые коэффициенты. Параллельная реализация использует MPI для распределения вычислений. Изображение делится по горизонтали на полосы строк между процессами с применением стратегии перекрытия границ (halo-обмен): каждый процесс получает дополнительные граничные строки от соседей для корректной обработки пикселей на стыках полос. После локального применения фильтра результаты собираются на процессе 0. author: copilot
body:
Agents needed a way to receive on-demand prompts at runtime and a general mechanism to observe what they are doing.

## Changes

### `Agent` interface additions
- **`Prompt(text string) <-chan *model.Response`** — non-blocking; spawns a goroutine that runs the prompt through the model (including tool execution), then delivers the response on a buffered channel and closes it. Channel is closed with no value if no model is configured.
- **`Activity() []Activity`** — returns a safe snapshot copy of the agent's activity log, capped at 256 entries.

### Activity tracking
- `ActivityType` string constants: `evaluate`, `prompt`, `tool`, `response`, `error`
- `Activity` struct: `Time`, `Type`, `Prompt`, `Tool`, `Result`, `Err`
- Internal `record()` helper — thread-safe, drops oldest entries beyond cap
- `evaluate()` now records each cycle's evaluate/tool/response/error events
- Tool call results are classified as `ActivityError` vs `ActivityTool` via JSON inspection of the content string

### Usage

```go
a := micro.NewAgent(
    agent.WithName("greeter-manager"),
    agent.WithModel(m),
    agent.WithDirective("Ensure greeter is healthy"),
)
go a.Run()

// Queue a prompt from any goroutine; non-blocking
ch := a.Prompt("how many nodes does greeter have?")
resp := <-ch // blocks only the caller, not the agent loop
fmt.Println(resp.Reply)

// Inspect recent activity
for _, act := range a.Activity() {
    fmt.Printf("[%s] %s %s\n", act.Time.Format(time.RFC3339), act.Type, act.Result)
}
```

body:
Adds voice-driven score input to the mobile scoring view. The referee dictates zone names aloud; the app recognises them in Finnish or English, speaks back a TTS confirmation, and announces series completion — all without touching the screen.

## New: `useVoiceScoring` hook

Manages a continuous `SpeechRecognition` session with stale-closure-safe refs. Exported `parseVoiceCommand` is pure and unit-testable.

```js
// Full Finnish + English zone vocabulary
VOICE_COMMANDS = {
  'X':  ['napa', 'napakymppi', 'x'],
  '10': ['kymmenen', 'kymppi', 'ten', '10'],
  '8':  ['kahdeksan', 'kasi', 'eight', '8'],
  'M':  ['ohi', 'ohilaukaus', 'miss', 'm'],
  // …all 12 zones
}
```

On each final recognition result, up to 3 alternatives are tried in confidence order; the first matching word wins. Zone confirmation is spoken via `SpeechSynthesis` and series completion is announced after an 800 ms delay so it does not overlap the zone utterance.

## `App.jsx` integration

- Hook called unconditionally at App scope (hooks rules); `voiceTotalShots` computed null-safe for non-scoring views.
- `useEffect` stops listening automatically on navigation away from scoring view.
- Scoring bottom bar gains a **microphone toggle**: green + pulsing animation when active, last-recognised zone shown inline. Falls back to an info note on browsers without Web Speech API.

## i18n

Five strings added to both `fi` and `en`: `voiceScoring`, `voiceNotSupported`, `voiceListening`, `voiceStart`, `voiceStop`.

## Tests

44 new unit tests for `parseVoiceCommand` — all 12 zones × Finnish/English, case insensitivity, multi-word transcripts, null/empty inputs.

### Motivation
- Provide a single, role-aware settings system that works for every membership role and fixes the "tenant setting not accessible" issue by using tenant/location context guards. 
- Separate common user profile settings from organization- and location-scoped settings so UI and APIs can enforce the correct context and permissions. 
- Ensure UI shows explicit "Not authorized" messages for blocked sections and that requests use `apiFetch` with the correct headers/context.

### Description
- Added backend endpoints under an authenticated surface: `GET/PATCH /api/users/me`, `POST /api/users/me/change-password`, `GET/PATCH /api/orgs/:id/settings`, and `GET/PATCH /api/gyms/:id/settings`, wired to a new role/context-aware `SettingsController` and extended `SettingsService`. 
- Enforced tenant/location membership and role checks by using `TenantGuard`, `LocationGuard`, and the membership `RolesGuard` with `RequireRoles` for org/location endpoints and explicit route-level ID checks that return `Not authorized` for mismatches.

## Motivation
The Gram regularization path currently relies on a separate Gram teacher model and extra scheduling knobs that add complexity and state without clear benefit for this workflow. We want a simpler Gram anchoring mechanism that uses the student's own stem features with stop-gradient semantics.

## Solution
Remove the dedicated Gram-teacher pipeline and compute Gram anchoring from masked, detached student stem outputs. Simplify JEPA configuration to only keep Gram controls that are still meaningful for the new anchor path.

## Changes
- Replace `gram_teacher_output` with `gram_anchor_output` in `MJEPAPredictions`.
- Replace Gram-teacher forward/update logic with `forward_gram_anchor`, which computes:
  `apply_mask(context_mask, student.stem(x), fill_value=None).detach()`
- Keep explicit stop-gradient in the Gram anchor path and add regression coverage for that behavior.
- Remove legacy JEPAConfig knobs and validation tied to Gram teacher snapshots/updates:
  - `gram_teacher_epoch`
  - `gram_update_interval_epoch`
  - `gram_resolution_scale`
- Remove now-obsolete helper functions (`forward_gram_teacher`, `is_gram_update_epoch`) from `mjepa/jepa.py`.
- Update default `config.yaml` to the new JEPAConfig shape.
- Update tests to align with anchor-only semantics and remove obsolete Gram-teacher lifecycle tests.
